title: Set up the workspace, runtime and shared tooling
what: A Bun and Turborepo workspace with one package or app per layer, a pinned Bun version, shared TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, knip, markdownlint, commitlint and lefthook configuration that each layer extends, and a root check command.
why: Every later story starts from the same checked, repeatable workspace, so a rule change happens in one place and developers get the same results locally and in CI.

criteria.says: Given a fresh checkout, when a developer runs `bun install` and `bun run check` at the root, then Turborepo runs lint, typecheck, test and build for every layer and exits with code 0.

Given the repository, when a developer lists the workspace, then the layers tooling, domain, contracts, data, api, ui, web and e2e each exist at their planned path and each extends the shared configuration without copying it.
Given a layer that imports a layer above it or leaves an export unused, when `bun run check` runs, then the check fails and names the import or export.

Given a commit with staged files that fail lint, format or typecheck, or a message that is not a conventional commit, when the developer commits, then lefthook rejects the commit and shows the failing check.

title: Fix the libraries every layer may use
what: The agreed libraries installed: Effect 4 with Schema, HttpApi, HttpClient and SQL; Drizzle ORM and Kit; fast-xml-parser; fflate; TanStack Query and Form; and the rule, written in AGENTS.md, that no library outside this stack is added without a story that needs it.
why: One schema language and a small, I/O-free parser set keep the Domain testable and avoid duplicate types, and nothing enters without a story that needs it.

criteria.says: Given the workspace after `bun install`, when a developer lists the installed dependencies, then Effect 4, Drizzle ORM, Drizzle Kit, fast-xml-parser, fflate, TanStack Query and TanStack Form are present and Zod is absent.
Given a dependency that is listed in a layer but never imported, or an export that nothing uses, when `bun run check` runs, then knip fails and names it.
Given the root AGENTS.md, when a developer reads it, then it states that no library outside the agreed stack is added without a story that needs it.

Given a small sample ADMX file and a small zip archive, when a Domain test parses the first with fast-xml-parser and unpacks the second with fflate in memory under Bun, then both succeed with no file, network or database access.

title: Configure environments, local database and the build version
what: Validated environment configuration with an .env.example, a Docker Compose file for local PostgreSQL, and a build step that reads the Git version and passes it to the services and screens as a declared Turborepo input.
why: Developers and the black-box tests run against the same database version, a missing setting stops the product at start-up, and the displayed version is never a stale committed file.

criteria.says: Given Docker is available, when a developer runs the documented compose command, then a PostgreSQL database starts and accepts a connection with the address given in .env.example.
Given an environment variable listed in .env.example is missing or invalid, when the service or the screens start, then they stop at start-up with a message naming the variable.
Given a Git checkout, when the product is built, then the Git version is available to the services and screens as a build-time value and no generated version file is added to the repository.
Given the Git version changes, when Turborepo builds again, then the affected tasks rerun instead of reusing a cached result.

title: Set up the test tooling for every layer
what: Vitest in each code layer, a real PostgreSQL test database for the Data layer, the HttpApi test client for the Services layer, Storybook stories for the components, Vitest tests of pure logic in the Screens layer, and Playwright with axe in the black-box layer.
why: A story can be called done only when its layer checks and its black-box test pass, and the tests catch what can really break: migrations, SQL behaviour and what a user sees.

criteria.says: Given a layer with a Vitest test, when `bun run test` runs, then Turborepo runs that layer's tests and reports a failing test as a failed task.

Given a table of sample ADMX, ADML, POL, REG, CMTX and SPOL files and a round-trip test for a parser and its writer, when the Domain tests run, then each sample is checked by an example-based test and the round-trip test passes.
Given the local database is running, when the Data tests run, then they connect to a real PostgreSQL test database, apply the migrations and use no in-memory fake.
Given a handler of the contract, when a Services test calls it through the HttpApi test client, then the test receives the handler's response without starting a network server.
Given a component, when Storybook is built, then the component's story renders and a component without a story is reported.
Given a pure function in the Screens layer, when the Screens tests run, then a Vitest test of that function runs and passes.
Given the running product and a seeded database, when Playwright runs a screen test, then axe checks that screen and any violation fails the test.
Given the project's CI, when it runs the Data tests and one Playwright test, then PostgreSQL starts under Docker and the Playwright browsers are available, and both tests run.

title: Set the pattern for rules written as tested code
what: One worked example in the Domain layer: a named, pure rule function with a test named after the rule, domain terms taken from the analysis wording, typed errors, and a round-trip test, plus the AGENTS.md lines that record the pattern; and the OpenAPI document and client generated from hand-written Contracts.
why: The legacy rules live as code and tests that cannot go stale silently, so every later story copies one proven pattern instead of inventing its own.

criteria.says: Given the example rule, when a developer reads the Domain layer, then the rule is one named pure function and its test carries the rule's name.
Given malformed input to the example parser, when it runs, then it returns a typed Effect error and an unknown element is kept and reported, not dropped.
Given text the example writer produced from the example parser's result, when it is compared with the original text, then the two match byte for byte where the format allows.

Given a hand-written schema and HttpApi group in Contracts, when the generate script runs, then the OpenAPI document and the client are written from them, and CI fails if the committed OpenAPI document differs from the generated one.
Given the AGENTS.md of each layer, when a developer reads it, then it states the layer's conventions and the reasons of the decisions that apply, and no separate wiki is needed.

title: Show the category tree and the list of a chosen category
what: Build the shared rules that decide which categories and policies are visible, how a category looks in the tree, and what the right pane lists for the chosen category.
why: Every screen that browses policies relies on the same visibility and listing rules, so they are built once and shared.

terms.name: Orphaned category
terms.means: A category whose definition names a parent that is not among the loaded definitions; not a category that simply has no parent.

terms.name: Empty category
terms.means: A category holding no subcategories and no policies at all, hidden ones included; not one whose policies are merely hidden by a filter.

criteria.says: Given a category whose definition names a parent that is not among the loaded definitions, when the category is assessed, then it is orphaned.
Given a category with no subcategories and no policies, hidden ones counted, when the category is assessed, then it is empty.
Given a category that is both orphaned and empty, when its icon is chosen, then the orphaned icon wins over the empty icon, which wins over the normal icon.
Given empty categories are switched off, when a category has no visible policy and no visible subcategory, then it is not visible; with them switched on it is always visible.

Given the user, computer or both areas are chosen, when a policy is assessed, then it is visible only if it applies to a chosen area, and with Only Filtered Policies on it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to, passing for either being enough.
Given the loaded categories, when the tree is shown, then only visible categories appear, each with its kind's icon and its visible subcategories below it, sorted.
Given a category is shown in the right pane, when the pane changes category, then the tree selection moves to that category.

Given a category is chosen, when the right pane lists it, then an Up row marked Parent with the parent's name comes first when a parent exists, then visible subcategories by name, then visible policies by name, each policy row showing its state and comment.
Given nothing is selected, when the description pane is shown, then the title and support lines are hidden and it reads "Select an item to see its description.".

title: Show a policy's state and comment per area
what: Build the shared rules that read a policy's state and comment in the user and computer areas, combine them when both areas are shown, and filter the list by state.
why: Administrators scan the policy list for what is configured, so state, comment and state filters must read the same way everywhere.

terms.name: Policy state
terms.means: Enabled, Disabled, Not Configured or Unknown for one area; not the policy's options.

criteria.says: Given a policy and an area, when its state is read, then it reads Enabled, Disabled, Not Configured or Unknown, from the computer source for the computer area and the user source for any other.

Given both areas are shown and the policy applies to both, when the states are shown, then the common state is followed by "(2)" when they match, the computer state by "(C)" when only the user is Not Configured, the user state by "(U)" when only the computer is Not Configured, and "Mixed" otherwise.

Given a state filter is chosen and an area is checked, when the list is filtered, then each policy's state is read in the checked area and only policies whose state matches remain: Configured keeps policies that are Enabled or Disabled, Not Configured keeps those that are Not Configured, and Disabled or Enabled keep only that state.
Given a policy and an area, when its comment is read, then it is empty when the source has no comment file or no comment for the policy, and otherwise the saved text.
Given both areas are shown, when the comment column is filled, then it is empty if neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" if both do, and otherwise shows the single comment.

title: Refuse invalid template files with clear messages
what: Build the shared rules that stop loading when a template or language file is invalid and tell the person what went wrong.
why: A broken template must never half-load silently; people need the reason and a choice about continuing.

terms.name: Template file
terms.means: An administrative template (ADMX) that defines categories, products, support rules and policies; not the language file (ADML) that supplies their text.

criteria.says: Given a template declares no target namespace, when the folder is loaded, then loading stops at once, later files are not read, nothing is built and the person sees the error text.

Given a template file cannot be parsed as XML, when it is loaded, then it is refused with "Couldn't load <path>: The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>.", and any other read problem is refused with "The ADMX is invalid: <detail>".

Given the chosen language file cannot be parsed as XML, when it is loaded, then the template is refused with "The ADML XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>", and any other read problem gives "The ADML is invalid: <detail>".
Given a language file repeats a text id in its first text table, when it is read, then it is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded; otherwise each text is kept under its id.

Given loading definitions reports problems, when loading ends, then the person sees "Errors were encountered while adding administrative templates to the workspace." with each problem and, only where a choice is wanted, is asked "Continue trying to use this workspace?"; with no problems nothing is shown.

title: Link loaded definitions into categories, products and policies
what: Build the shared rules that resolve names, references and text across loaded templates and assemble the final lists of categories, products, support rules and policies.
why: Templates refer to each other and to language text by name, so people only see a coherent catalogue if every reference resolves the same way.

terms.name: Reference
terms.means: A name in one template that points to a category, product or support rule, possibly in another template; not the policy's own text.

terms.name: Settings screen layout
terms.means: The arrangement of controls a policy shows for its options; not the options' registry effects.

criteria.says: Given a name or description written as "$(string.<id>)", when it is shown, then it shows the language file's text for that id, an unknown id shows the code itself, other text is shown as written and an empty value stays empty.

Given a reference with a colon, when it is resolved, then it uses the namespace declared for its prefix, an unknown prefix is taken as already complete, and a reference without a colon belongs to the template's own namespace.

Given a category names a parent, when definitions are built, then it is attached under that parent found in this load or earlier ones, and when the parent is not found it has no parent but is still listed among the top-level categories.
Given a support rule entry, when it is linked, then it links to the product its reference names, else to the support rule of that name, else stays unlinked.

Given a policy names a category, when definitions are built, then it is listed under that category found in this load or earlier ones, and when not found it stays in the policy list but belongs to no category.
Given a policy names a support rule, when it is built, then it shows the rule found in this load or earlier ones, and when none is found it has none.

Given a policy names a settings screen layout, when it is built, then it gets a layout only if the name is written "$(presentation.<id>)" and the language file holds a layout with that id, and otherwise has none.

Given the structures are built, when loading finishes, then all new categories, products, support rules and policies join the final lists and the staged items are cleared, so later files add to what is available.

title: Read policies, products and options from template files
what: Build the shared rules that turn a template file into categories, products, registry values, policies and typed options, including the defaults for missing attributes.
why: The policy catalogue is only as correct as its reading of Microsoft's templates, so each reading rule is built once and tested.

terms.name: Policy option
terms.means: An input a policy offers when enabled, such as a number, text, yes/no, list or choice; not the policy's enabled or disabled state.

terms.name: Product
terms.means: A product, its major versions and their minor versions that policies are supported on; not a policy.

criteria.says: Given a category carries any content, even only a comment, when the template is read, then it must contain a parent entry with a reference, otherwise the template is refused as invalid; a category holding only a comment still needs that parent entry; its explanation is optional.

Given products in a template, when they are read, then three levels are kept (product, major versions, minor versions), deeper levels are not read, and a version without a version index makes the file invalid.
Given a registry value in a template, when it is read, then it is a delete marker, a number or a text by the first of those it contains, and a value with none is a delete marker.

Given a policy, when it is read, then its switched-on and switched-off effects come from its enabled and disabled values and lists, each list entry naming a value and optionally its own key, else the list's default key.
Given a policy, when it is read, then its category and support rule come from the references in its own content and it has options only if it contains an options section.
Given a policy option of a kind other than number, yes/no, text, list, choice or multi-line text, when it is read, then it is dropped without notice.

Given a number option, when it is read, then it accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295 unless limits are set, overwrites existing values unless soft, is stored as a number unless text, and unreadable attributes fall back to these defaults.

Given a text option, when it is read, then it allows 255 characters, is optional, is stored as plain text and overwrites existing values unless the template says otherwise, with unreadable attributes falling back to these defaults.
Given a yes/no option, when it is read, then its registry effect for true and false comes from true and false values and lists.

Given a choice option, when it is read, then it is optional unless required, each choice keeps a single registry value, a list of values or both, and a choice with neither is accepted and changes nothing.

Given an option, when its registry value name is chosen, then it is its own value name, except for a list option with a value prefix attribute (even if empty), which uses the prefix and falls back to its own name only when the prefix is empty.

title: Read settings screen layouts from language files
what: Build the shared rules that read the controls of a policy's settings screen from a language file, with their defaults.
why: People set policy options through these controls, so each starts in the state Microsoft's language file intends.

terms.name: Control
terms.means: One input or label on a policy's settings screen; not the registry value it writes.

criteria.says: Given a screen layout in a language file, when it is read, then only labels, number boxes, text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, drop-down lists, list boxes and multi-line text boxes are kept and any other control is dropped without notice.

Given a number box, when it is read, then it has default value 1, shows its spinner and steps by 1 unless the language file says otherwise, and an unreadable attribute value falls back to the same defaults.
Given a check box, when it is shown, then it starts unticked unless the language file marks it ticked.
Given a combo box or drop-down list, when its entries are shown, then they are sorted unless the language file says not to sort them.
Given a drop-down list, when it is shown, then an item is preselected only when the language file names one, otherwise none is.

title: Work out whether a policy is enabled or disabled from its values
what: Build the shared rules that weigh the registry values of a policy as evidence that it is enabled or disabled.
why: A policy's state is not stored; it is read from values, so every screen must reach the same verdict from the same values.

terms.name: Evidence
terms.means: A registry value found present or marked for deletion that counts toward a policy being enabled or disabled; not the final state itself.

criteria.says: Given a policy with a registry value of its own, when it is assessed, then it is enabled evidence when the value holds its on value (the number 1 when the template gives none), and disabled evidence when it holds its off value or, when the template gives none, is marked for deletion.
Given the policy's lists of on-values and off-values, when they are assessed, then each present value counts as enabled or disabled evidence, using the list's own key when it names one.
Given a policy's list element, when it is assessed, then a list marked for deletion counts as one deleted element and a list holding any values counts as a present element and cancels that deletion.
Given a number, text, choice or multi-line text element, when it is assessed, then a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a present value counts as a present element.

Given the elements of a policy, when evidence is added, then if any element is present their count is added to the enabled evidence, and only when none is present do deleted elements add to the disabled evidence.

title: Decide whether a policy's support rules are met
what: Build the shared rules that decide whether the products a policy is supported on are chosen, through support rules, version ranges and nested rules.
why: People filter policies by the Windows products they run, so a policy must count as supported exactly as the legacy product decided.

terms.name: Support rule
terms.means: A named group of product entries that says where a policy is supported, with all-of or any-of logic; not a single product.

criteria.says: Given a support entry for a product with versions beneath it, when it is checked, then it is met when any version in its range (minimum 0 if none, maximum the highest if none) or a sub-product directly beneath one is chosen, a range entry never matches its own product, and a product with no versions never matches this way.

Given a support definition with entries, when it is checked, then with 'any' asked an all-of definition needs every entry met and any other needs one, without 'any' one entry meets every definition, a definition with no or no met entries is met only when all are required, and plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.
Given a support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation, when it is checked, then it counts as not met, so two entries pointing at the same definition make the second one not met.

title: Read and list values in policy files and registry policy keys
what: Build the shared rules that decide which values a policy file or policy registry key holds, which are marked for deletion and which keys count as policy keys.
why: Editing and saving policies depends on reading present and deleted values exactly as Group Policy files record them.

terms.name: Marked for deletion
terms.means: A value a policy file records as to be removed when applied; not a value that is simply absent.

terms.name: Policy key
terms.means: A registry key within one of the three policy branches; not any registry key.

criteria.says: Given a policy file, when a value is checked, then it is marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, the key has a clear-all marker, or a delete-values list for the key names it, regardless of case; entries are examined in sorted order, and a value sorting after the marker is stored as present and cancels the deletion, whenever it was written and whichever marker kind came first.
Given a policy file, when a value is checked for presence, then it is present only if stored and not marked for deletion.
Given a policy file, when a value is read, then nothing is returned when it is absent or marked for deletion.
Given a key in a policy file, when its values are listed, then marker entries are left out unless the caller asks for them.
Given a registry key, when it is judged, then it counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches or below one, regardless of case.

Given an imported registry source, when a value is checked for presence, then it is present when its key exists and, unless the name is empty, lists a value of that name regardless of case, an empty name meaning the key itself.
Given an imported registry source, when a value is checked for deletion, then it is never reported as marked for deletion.

title: Detect the Group Policy edition and read optional attributes
what: Build two small shared rules: deciding from an edition number whether a Windows edition has the Group Policy infrastructure, and reading an XML attribute that may be absent. The decisions make the service server rendered with no sight of the user's machine and name no place where the edition is read, so the number is an input the rule receives; which source supplies it is not decided and is left to the product owner.
why: Keeps one tested rule for whether an edition counts as having Group Policy infrastructure, and keeps template reading from failing on optional data. The legacy reason for the edition check (telling people whether built-in Group Policy is available) is not part of the rule itself.

criteria.says: Given an edition number supplied to the rule (0 when none could be obtained), when it equals one of the 59 fixed edition codes, then the edition counts as having the Group Policy infrastructure; otherwise, including 0, it counts as having none. The rule reads no machine itself, because the service cannot see the user's machine; where the number comes from is not decided and is flagged to the product owner.
Given an XML attribute that is absent, when it is read, then nothing is returned.

title: Load policy templates from an uploaded package with the right language
what: Domain rules that take an uploaded template package (a set of named files, some in language subfolders) and pick its template files and the language file for each, load them as pairs and keep the loaded set apart from any earlier one. The service reads no folder of the person's machine; the package arrives by upload and its files are stored by Data.
why: Every later story reads policies from the loaded definitions, so loading must be exact about what it takes, refuses and reports.

terms.name: Template file
terms.means: An ADMX file that defines policies, categories, products and support rules; not the language file that carries their text.

terms.name: Language file
terms.means: The ADML file that holds the text of one template in one language; not the template itself.

terms.name: Template package
terms.means: The set of template files and language subfolders a person uploads (or the service downloads from Microsoft) to load definitions; not a single template file.

criteria.says: Given an uploaded template package holding files with names ending in .admx in any letter case at its top level, entries in subfolders and other files, when the package is loaded, then only the top-level .admx files are taken as templates; subfolder entries and other files are ignored.

Given a template and the language subfolders of the uploaded package, when its language file is chosen, then the subfolder named exactly by the language code wins if it holds this template's file, else the first subfolder whose name starts with the same language part (before the dash, capital letters mattering) that holds it, else the en-US subfolder if it holds it; a subfolder lacking the file is skipped. The choice works on the names of the uploaded files, never on a folder of the machine.
Given no language file in any of those places, when the template is loaded, then it is refused with "The corresponding ADML is missing" and none of its content is loaded.

Given a template whose namespace an earlier template already holds, when it is loaded, then it is refused with "The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file", so one file cannot be added twice.

Given an uploaded package where some templates are refused with a reported failure (unparsable, invalid, namespace already owned, or no usable language file), when it is loaded, then each failure is listed, the other templates still load and the structures are built from those that did.

Given a template and its language file both load, when the build runs, then its categories, products, support rules and policies are staged and the pair is recorded as loaded under the template's namespace.
Given no saved language code, when definition text is needed, then the computer's own language is used; otherwise the saved code is used.
Given loaded definitions and earlier search results, when the workspace is closed or replaced, then all definitions and the previous search results are discarded.

title: Validate template and language files while reading them
what: Domain parsing rules that read a template and its language file into typed definitions and refuse the file as invalid when required parts are missing or malformed.
why: A malformed file must be refused with a reason instead of loading half of its content.

criteria.says: Given a template file, when it is read, then it is refused as invalid if any of these is missing or unreadable: the policy definitions section; a namespace entry's prefix or namespace; a superseded-ADM file name; a minimum revision (missing or not a number); a support rule's name or display name; a support reference or range without its reference, or a version bound that is not a whole number; a product's name, display name or version index; a category's name or display name; a category's parent entry, or the parent's reference when the category has content; a policy's name, display name, key or class; a policy's category or supported-on reference; a number value's value; a list item's value name; a choice item's display name; or an option's id.
Given a superseded entry without a file name or a minimum revision that is absent or not a number, when the template is read, then it is refused as invalid; when present they are read.
Given a template that lists a target namespace and declares prefixes, when it is read, then the namespace is the one listed as its target, and a prefix declared twice refuses the file as invalid.
Given a language file with no policy resources section or a revision that is missing or not a number, when it is read, then it is refused as invalid and its template is not loaded.
Given a language file with several presentation tables, when it is read, then screen layouts come only from the first table, and a layout id that appears twice refuses the file as invalid.
Given a control in a language file, when it is read, then it keeps the reference id the file gives it, tying it to the matching option in the template, or has no id when none is given.
Given an XML attribute that is absent or whose text is invalid for the type of its default, when it is read, then the default is used.
Given items from two templates with equal names, when each is named, then its unique name is its namespace, a colon and its name, so they stay apart.

title: Read support rules, products, classes and list options from templates
what: Domain rules that turn template content into support rules, a product tree, the computer or user area of each policy and list options.
why: Support filtering and editing depend on these definitions being read the way the legacy product reads them.

criteria.says: Given a support rule, when it is read, then it is 'any of' for a first logic element "or", 'all of' for "and", blank otherwise, only that first element is read, and a range may carry a minimum and maximum version.
Given child products attached to parents, when products are built, then each child sits under its parent defined in the same template and only parentless products are top-level.
Given a policy class of "Machine", "User" or any other value, when it is read, then it applies to computers, users, or both respectively.
Given a policy declared for an area or for both, when areas are checked, then it applies to the declared area and a policy declared for both applies to each.

Given a list option, when it is read, then it replaces other entries of its key unless additive, stores plain text unless expandable, numbers entries automatically unless the template says the person names them, and is prefixed only when a value prefix is given.

title: Decide whether a policy is enabled, disabled or unsupported
what: Domain rules that weigh the stored values of a policy to give its state, tell preferences from managed policies and check support against chosen products.
why: People rely on the state shown for a policy; it must match what the legacy product reports.

criteria.says: Given enabled and disabled evidence, when the state is decided, then it is Enabled if enabled exceeds disabled, Disabled if the reverse, Not configured with none, and Unclear when both are equal and above zero.

Given a checkbox element, when evidence is counted, then a value marked for deletion counts one deleted element; otherwise each present off value or off-list value counts a tenth of a deleted element and each present on value or on-list value counts one present element; a checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence, even if it holds 1.

Given a stored value, when it is checked as present, then a deletion marker must be marked for deletion, a number must be a whole number equal to the expected one, text must equal the expected text, and a value of the wrong kind is not present.

Given a policy naming a registry key outside software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies and system\currentcontrolset\policies, when it is classified, then it is a preference, otherwise a managed policy.
Given a policy listing no supported-on information or an entry naming no known product, when support is checked, then it counts as supported only if unlisted policies are allowed.
Given a support entry for a product, when it is checked, then it is met if it is not a version range and that exact product is chosen, or if any version or sub-product beneath the product is chosen.

title: Read and write policy files with a byte-faithful round trip
what: Domain parsing and writing of POL files, with the typing of stored values. A POL file arrives by upload and leaves as a download (integrations.decision-1).
why: Policy files must be read and saved without loss or surprise, because people overwrite real policy files with the output.

terms.name: POL file
terms.means: A Registry.pol policy file that holds registry keys and values for computers or users; not a REG file, which is text.

criteria.says: Given a policy file that does not start with the 'PReg' signature, when it is read, then it is refused with 'Missing PReg signature'.
Given a policy file whose format version is not 1, when it is read, then it is refused with 'Unknown (newer) version of POL format'.
Given the same key and value name twice, when the file is read, then the later entry wins, names match regardless of letter case and the first spelling seen is kept for saving.
Given text or a multiple-string value, when it is read, then text stops at its first empty character and a multiple-string value ends at its first empty string.

Given a stored value, when it is read back, then text and expandable text give text, numbers give 32-bit or 64-bit numbers, multiple strings give a list of strings and every other type gives raw bytes.

Given a policy file read without change, when it is written back, then its bytes are identical wherever the legacy format allows; a value is written as the type it was read as, and an unknown element is kept and reported rather than dropped.

title: Open policy sources from imported files and describe them
what: Domain rules (with the imported content stored by Data) for each kind of policy source: how it is opened from an uploaded POL or REG file, whether it can be changed, how it is named and how it is closed. Live registry access, loaded user hives and Active Directory are not carried; they become import and export of files (integrations.decision-2, integrations.decision-7, scope.decision-12).
why: People choose where policies come from; each source must open, report and close predictably, with files in place of the Windows registry.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: The place user or computer policy values are read from and saved to; in this product always an imported file or an empty working copy, not the live system.

terms.name: Registry source
terms.means: A source filled from an imported REG file in place of the Windows registry; not a live view of the machine's registry.

terms.name: Local GPO
terms.means: The computer's own Group Policy, brought in as its Registry.pol file by upload; not a domain policy.

terms.name: User GPO
terms.means: A person's Group Policy object (a policy set held in the domain for that person), brought in as its Registry.pol file by upload (integrations.decision-7).

terms.name: User hive
terms.means: A person's saved registry settings file, brought in as a REG file; not a registry loaded into the machine.

terms.name: SID
terms.means: The security identifier that names a person's account; a User hive source may show it in brackets.

terms.name: Scratch space
terms.means: An empty working copy of policies that can be changed but is never saved anywhere; not any file.

criteria.says: Given an imported REG file whose keys do not start with HKCU, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKU, HKEY_USERS, HKLM or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (any letter case), when it is opened as a registry source, then it is refused with "The root key is not valid."; a path after the root is opened, and created in the working copy if missing. No live registry key is opened.

Given an uploaded POL file (a POL file, the local Group Policy or a user's Group Policy object, each as a Registry.pol file), when it is opened, then its content is loaded into a stored working copy that can be changed and is saved by download; the legacy check that the file on disk can be opened for reading and writing does not apply because no file on a machine is held open.

Given a user hive imported as a REG file, when it is opened, then its content is loaded as a source with no mounting, temporary name or privileges; if the file cannot be read, the source becomes an empty, read-only scratch source without telling the person.
Given a Scratch space source, when it is opened, then it is an empty store that can be changed and is never saved.

Given a registry source filled from an imported file, when writability is checked, then it is changeable as a working copy and nothing is ever written to or removed from a machine registry; saving is an export of a REG or POL file.

Given a source, when its name is shown, then it is Local GPO, Registry, File, User GPO, User hive or Scratch space, followed in brackets by the name of the imported file (in place of a path or SID) when there is one.

Given a number or text in an imported REG file, when a value is read from the registry source, then a missing key gives nothing, a number is held as the unsigned number policies use and environment variables in text are not expanded; no live registry is read.

Given an unsigned 32-bit or 64-bit number in a registry source, when it is exported to a REG or POL file, then it is written with the same bits the registry would store as its signed number and the key is created in the export if missing; no live registry is written.
Given a source being closed, when it is a user hive source, then there is nothing to unload and closing succeeds, as it does for every other kind of source; no hive is mounted or unloaded.
Given sources closing where one could not release its resources, when closing ends, then the person is told "Cleanup did not complete fully because the loaded resources are open in other programs."

title: Refuse operations a REG file source cannot support
what: Domain rules that make a REG file source fail every read-style request with 'not implemented'.
why: Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file must fail visibly rather than give wrong answers.

criteria.says: Given a REG file source, when a value is asked for presence, read, checked for deletion or a key's values are listed, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.

title: Keep policy comments with their source and read comment files
what: Domain rules (with comments stored by Data next to the policy state they belong to) for where a source's comments live and when a comment file is unreadable; a comment file (CMTX) is only imported and exported (integrations.decision-6).
why: Comments must stay with their source and a damaged file must not give partial comments.

terms.name: Comment file
terms.means: A CMTX file holding the comments written on policies; here an import and export format, not where comments are kept.

criteria.says: Given a source, when its comments are kept, then they are stored with that source in Data and not in any file beside it; when exported as a comment file, it is named like the source's file with the extension .cmtx, or comment.cmtx for the local or a user's Group Policy source; a registry source has no beside-the-file location and its export name is chosen at download; Scratch space has no comments, so comments are unavailable.

Given a comment file where any policy reference has no colon or an undeclared prefix, text is not "$(resource.<id>)", a text id is missing or two comments resolve to the same policy, when it is read, then no comment is read.
Given the comments of a source, when they are exported as a comment file and imported again, then the same comments come back and the text is byte-faithful where the format allows.

title: Show category and policy details and keep the list tidy
what: Rules for what the information pane, icons and state column show, and how selection survives a rebuild.
why: People browse the definitions by what the pane tells them.

criteria.says: Given a selected or highlighted category, when the pane shows it, then it gives the title, "This category contains N policies and M subcategories." ("The selected category" when only highlighted) and its explanation, counting hidden items too.

Given a selected policy, when the pane shows it, then it gives the title, "(no requirements information)" or "Requirements:" plus the support name, its explanation, and a preference notice only for preferences.
Given a policy description, when it is shown, then leading and trailing spaces of every line are removed and trailing blank space is dropped.
Given a policy, when its icon is chosen, then it is preference first, plain when it has no configurable elements, else "extra configuration".
Given both areas shown, when a policy's state is displayed, then a policy applying to one area shows its state followed by "(C)" or "(U)"; with a single area only the state is shown.
Given the category tree rebuilt from loaded definitions, when it finishes, then nothing is selected and the pane shows the empty state.

Given a rebuilt list, when the earlier policy is still in the category shown and passes the visibility rule, then it is selected and revealed, otherwise nothing is selected; the earlier top row is restored if the policy is in the same category and the list has that many rows.

title: Filter policies and keep search results
what: Rules for the filters of the policy list and the life of the search results.
why: People narrow a large list of policies by managed or preference, comment and product.

criteria.says: Given a filter on managed policies, when it is applied, then preferences are hidden when managed policies are wanted and managed policies are hidden when preferences are wanted.
Given several active filter parts, when a policy is tested, then it passes only if it passes every active part.
Given a filter on comments, when it is applied, then it keeps only policies with a non-empty comment in the checked area, or only those with none, as chosen.
Given a filter on products, when it is applied, then it keeps only policies supported by the chosen products, honouring the options to match any product and to include blank support.
Given search results, when the search is cleared, then the results are forgotten and reopening them reports that no search has been run.

title: Resolve where each policy source comes from and whether it can be saved
what: Decide where each kind of policy source gets its content (an uploaded file or stored data, never a folder on the service's machine) and describe whether it can be written, starting a missing source empty.
why: Every source is opened from a known origin and people are told plainly when changes cannot be kept.

criteria.says: Given a source kind, when its origin is resolved, then a POL file, a local-policy file, a per-user policy object and an imported registry or user-hive file each take the file the person uploads, the service reads no user folder and makes no directory connection, and scratch space has no origin.

Given no policy file has been uploaded for a source, when it is opened, then an empty source is created in the stored data and treated as writable, nothing is created on disk and no person identifier is looked up, so a mistyped identifier creates nothing; if creating the empty source fails, an empty read-only source is used and no error is shown.

Given a source, when its writability is decided, then scratch space is writable, a registry-style source is 'no writing' when the write test failed, and others are 'no commit' when the file could not be opened for writing.

Given a source, when its writability is described, then it reads 'is fully writable', 'cannot be saved' (changes work in memory only) or 'cannot be modified', and anything but fully writable counts as a problem.

title: Open policy sources, load their comments and report the result
what: Open the user and computer sources together, close the previous ones first, load each source's stored comments and tell the person how it went.
why: People know what was discarded, which comments are available and whether everything can be saved.

criteria.says: Given sources are already open, when new sources are opened, then the old ones are closed first and unsaved changes are discarded for file-backed and empty sources, while registry-style sources lose nothing.

Given a source is opened, when its comments are loaded, then they come from the comments stored with that source (filled by importing a CMTX file), no folder or file location is created or read, a source with none stored has no comments yet, and any failure leaves the source without comments.

Given a comment file, when it is read, then it is refused as unreadable if it lacks a comment-definitions section, has a namespace entry without a prefix, a comment without a policy reference, a text without an id, or repeats a prefix, policy reference or text id, and its comments are unavailable.

Given sources have just opened, when either is not fully writable, then the person is told 'Not all policy sources are fully writable.' with the state of the user and computer source; when both are writable the confirmation appears only if opening was not quiet, never at start.

title: Read and write the stored form of values in a policy file
what: Read a policy file leniently and write it back with entries in order and values encoded as the format requires.
why: Files saved by Policy Plus are accepted by Windows and read back unchanged.

criteria.says: Given a policy file with an extra empty character after a value name, when it is read, then the character is skipped.
Given a policy file, when it is saved, then entries are written alphabetically so a key-clearing marker precedes the values it clears.
Given a value, when it is written, then text, expandable text, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers and multiple strings use their own encoding, and every other type is stored as raw bytes with its type.
Given text, when it is stored, then it is two-byte characters followed by a closing empty character.
Given a multiple-string value, when it is stored, then each string is followed by an empty character and one more empty character closes the list.
Given a 32-bit number, when it is stored, then it is 4 bytes, lowest byte first.
Given a 64-bit number, when it is stored, then it is 8 bytes, lowest byte first.

title: Set, delete and forget values and key clearances in a policy file
what: Change a policy file's entries: set a value, mark it deleted, forget it, clear a key and forget the clearance.
why: Edits to a policy file leave it in the same state Microsoft's tools would.

criteria.says: Given a value is set, when it is stored, then it replaces any value held under that name and a deletion marker for the name is not removed.
Given a value is marked for deletion, when it is stored, then any held value or marker under the name is dropped and a marker holding 32 is added unless already marked or its key is cleared.
Given a value is forgotten, when it is stored, then both the value and its deletion marker are removed so the policy says nothing about it.
Given a key is cleared, when it is stored, then all values and markers under it are dropped and a single clear-all marker is kept.
Given a key's clearance is forgotten, when it is stored, then every clear-all marker for that key is removed.

title: Apply one policy file's changes to another source
what: Apply the entries of a policy file onto another source, including delete and clear instructions and dropped values of an older file.
why: Importing a policy file gives the same result as the legacy product.

criteria.says: Given an entry, when applied, then it is saved only if its value name is non-empty and does not start with '**'; other marker or empty-named entries are skipped without notice, and a saved value keeps its case and type.

Given an entry named '**del.' plus a value name, when applied, then that value is deleted using lower-case key and value names; '**deletevalues' deletes each value in its semicolon-separated list likewise.
Given an entry starting '**delvals', when applied, then the whole key is cleared by its lower-case name, entries being applied in sorted order so clear-all comes before values.

Given an entry starting '**deletekeys', when applied, then each key in its semicolon-separated list under the entry's key is cleared by lower-case name, removing only that key's own values and not its subkeys.
Given a newer file applied over an older one, when applied, then values the old file held and the new dropped are forgotten in the target, only under the three policy branches.

title: Replace live registry changes with the registry source model
what: Give the registry-style source its delete, forget and clear behaviour in the Domain, filled from imported files.
why: The same edits work on a registry source without touching a real machine registry.

criteria.says: Given a value is deleted and its key does not exist, when the deletion runs, then nothing happens and no error is raised.
Given a value is forgotten in a registry source, when it runs, then the value is deleted, as a pending deletion cannot be remembered.
Given a key is cleared in a registry source, when it runs, then every value in it is deleted, the key and subkeys stay, and forgetting a clearance does nothing.

title: Edit entries of a REG file within its source branch
what: Save, delete, clear and forget values and keys in a REG file, limited to a source branch when one is set.
why: Registry files can be imported, edited and exported without stray changes.

criteria.says: Given a value is saved, when it runs, then it is ignored if a source branch is set and the key is outside it, otherwise any value under that name is replaced.
Given a value is deleted, when it runs, then it is ignored if outside the branch or the key is already marked for removal, otherwise it is recorded as deleted.
Given a key is cleared, when it runs, then it is ignored if outside the branch, otherwise earlier entries are replaced by a key-removal entry.
Given a key's clearance is forgotten, when it runs, then the key-removal entry is dropped if present, ignored if outside the branch.
Given a value is forgotten, when it runs on a REG file, then the request fails as 'not implemented', so applying a newer file over an older one fails for any dropped value under a policy branch.

title: Read a policy's saved state from its stored values
what: Read each kind of policy element and checkbox from the values stored in a source.
why: A policy shows the same Enabled options as the legacy product.

criteria.says: Given a number or text element, when read, then the saved value is taken as stored without checking it exists or its kind.
Given a multi-line text element, when read, then its value is taken as stored without checking existence.
Given a checkbox, when read, then it is on when its on value or all its on list is present, or value 1 when none is defined, and off otherwise including when the off value is present.
Given a list of values, when checked, then it counts as present only when every value is present.
Given a choice element, when read, then it is the position of the first item whose value is present and whose list is wholly present, or -1.
Given a list element with names the person provides, when read, then it is every stored name with its value under the element's key.
Given a list element whose names do not matter, when read, then with a prefix it is prefix1, prefix2 and so on until the first missing number, otherwise every stored value name under the key.

title: Forget a policy and list the registry values it touches
what: Work out every registry value a policy touches and drop them all when it is forgotten.
why: Not configured really means the source says nothing about the policy.

criteria.says: Given a policy, when its touched values are listed, then they are its own value, its value lists, its elements' values (whole key for list elements) and checkbox and choice sub-lists, each once.
Given a policy is forgotten, when it runs, then each list element's whole key is cleared and every touched value is dropped so it reads as Not configured.

title: Keep the browser view consistent after view or edit changes
what: Move to the nearest visible category and refresh the list after a view setting or an accepted edit.
why: People are never left on a hidden category or a stale list.

criteria.says: Given a view setting changes, when applied, then the view moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if moved or hidden, rebuilds tree and list, and a kept policy shows in the information pane only, not highlighted.
Given an edit dialog is accepted, when it closes, then the list refreshes in place if the category is visible, otherwise moves to the nearest visible one, and nothing is written to disk until Save.

title: Show the SPOL fragment with an optional header
what: Show a policy's SPOL fragment with the header only when asked.
why: People can copy a fragment alone or a complete SPOL document.

criteria.says: Given the fragment is shown, when 'Include SPOL header' is ticked, then the text starts with 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy' and a blank line; otherwise only the fragment appears.

title: Describe products and support definitions in their detail views
what: Give the product and support detail views their labels, versions, parents, children and matching wording.
why: People understand what a product or support definition covers.

criteria.says: Given a product, when details open, then it is labelled 'Major revision', 'Minor revision' or 'Top-level product' and shows a version only for major and minor revisions.

Given a product, when details open, then a parent shows its name with the parent button enabled, none shows blank and disabled, and all child revisions are listed with version and name, empty if none.
Given a support definition, when details open, then it states 'Match all the referenced products', 'Match any of the referenced products' or 'Do not match products'.

Given a support definition entry, when listed, then it is named by the nested definition, else the product, else '<missing: ' plus the product code; versions are listed only for product entries naming a range, a missing bound blank.

title: Stamp each build with its current Git version
what: When a build is made, the program is stamped with the version that Git gives for the current commit, so the screens and the service can report which version they are. Each run replaces the previous stamp; the stamp is not kept in the repository.
why: People who run or support Policy Plus can tell exactly which commit a build came from, and releases always carry the right version without anyone editing a file by hand.

terms.name: Build version
terms.means: The text Git gives to describe the commit a build was made from, shown as the program's version; it is not a hand-written release number.

criteria.says: Given a Git checkout with a current commit, when a build or the release workflow runs, then the program carries as its version the value taken from Git for that commit, replacing the version of any earlier run.

Given a checkout with tags, when the version is stamped, then it is the text Git's describe command gives (a tag, with commit count and short commit name when the commit is not itself tagged), and given a checkout without tags, then it is the short commit name.
Given the repository as committed, when anyone looks for a generated version file, then none is committed and the version reaches the service and the screens only as a value passed at build time.

Given the Git version changes, when the build is run again, then the build runs afresh with the new version instead of reusing an earlier result, because the Git version is a declared input of the build.

open: What should a build outside a Git checkout, with no version supplied by the release workflow, show as its version?

title: Open the download window and name where the definitions go
what: A person opens the window for getting Microsoft's policy definitions and sees where the downloaded definitions will be kept, with the same fixed starting point every time.
why: So a person who lacks the full set of policy definitions can start the download from a window that is always ready and needs no folder knowledge.

terms.name: Policy definitions
terms.means: The template files, with their language files, that describe every policy the program can show; not the policy settings a person has chosen.

criteria.says: Given the person opens the download window, when it appears, then it shows that Microsoft's package will be kept as the program's policy definitions, the same each time it opens, and no new set of definitions is offered to the screen that opened it until a download has finished and the person agrees to use it.

Given the window is open, when the person looks for a folder to choose, then there is none: the service reads no folder of the person, so the destination cannot be replaced by choosing one and cancelling changes nothing.

title: Stop a second download and closing while a download runs
what: While a download is running, the person cannot start another one, cannot change anything about it and cannot close the window; everything is available again when it ends.
why: So a download is never started twice or cut off half way, which would leave the definitions in an unknown state.

criteria.says: Given a download is running, when the person tries to close the window, then the close is refused and the window stays open; given no download is running, when the person closes the window, then it closes.

Given a download is running, when the person looks at the window, then the start and close buttons are disabled, so a second download cannot be started, and they are enabled again when the download ends, whether it succeeded or failed. The destination box and the browse button the old program also disabled are not carried, because there is no folder to choose.

title: Download and install Microsoft's policy definitions
what: The person starts the download; the service fetches Microsoft's fixed policy template package, unpacks it, stores the template files and language files as the program's definitions, and tells the person whether it worked and offers to open them.
why: So someone on an edition without the full set of policy definitions can get Microsoft's current ones in one step.

terms.name: Template package
terms.means: The single Microsoft download that holds the template files and their language files; not the definitions already stored in the program.

terms.name: Format language
terms.means: The language of the person's regional settings, which can differ from the language the program is shown in.

journey.name: Get Microsoft's policy definitions
steps: Open the download window
Start the download
Wait while the package is fetched and unpacked
Read the result
Choose to open the new definitions or not

criteria.says: Given the person starts the download, when it runs, then the service fetches the one fixed package, the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2) administrative templates, from the configured Microsoft address, and the person cannot choose another version.

Given the package was fetched, when the service unpacks it, then the template files and their language files are ready to store; if unpacking fails the person is told "Failed to extract the package." and nothing is stored.

Given the files were unpacked, when they are stored, then the template files are stored, then the language files for the person's format language are stored under that language if the package holds them, and unless that language is en-US the English files are also stored as the fallback; if the package holds no English files the person is told "Failed to move the ADMX files."

Given definitions with the same file names are already stored, when the new ones are stored, then each is replaced by the new one with no backup, and only files at the top level of the package are stored.

Given the service stores files for the person, when it runs, then it takes no ownership of any folder and sets no permissions, because there is no folder of the person and the "Failed to take control of the destination." message cannot occur.

Given a step fails (making room to work, downloading, unpacking, storing, or tidying up), when the person is told, then the message reads "Failed to " followed by that step, the window stays open, the controls are enabled again and no new definitions are offered; if only the final tidying of the working space fails, all definitions are already stored yet the person is told "Failed to remove temporary files." and no new definitions are offered.

Given the download succeeded, when the working space is cleared, then the person is asked "ADMX files downloaded successfully. Open them now?" and the new definitions are offered to the screen only on Yes; either answer closes the window as done.

open: The old program unpacked a Windows installer file (W11Admx.msi) with the Windows installer tool, which the server cannot run and an archive library cannot open: how should the service unpack this package?
The old program could leave some definitions replaced and others not when storing failed part way: should storing now be all or nothing, or may it stop part way as before?

title: Offer the download once, on first run, when definitions are incomplete
what: The first time the program is shown, it offers to download Microsoft's policy definitions if the loaded ones look incomplete, and never considers the offer again.
why: So a new person on an edition without the full definitions is led to the download, without being asked again on every visit.

terms.name: Welcome offer
terms.means: The one-time question on first run whether to download Microsoft's definitions; not the Help menu item that does the same at any time.

terms.name: Orphaned category
terms.means: A category whose definition names a parent that is not among the loaded definitions; not a category that is merely empty.

journey.name: First run with incomplete definitions
steps: Open the program for the first time
Read the welcome offer
Choose Yes to open the download window

criteria.says: Given the offer has not been considered, when the screen is shown, then the program records that it was considered, even when no offer is made, and never considers it again.

Given the offer is considered, the computer has no Group Policy support, and more than two non-empty categories name a parent that is not among the loaded definitions, when the screen is shown, then the person sees "Welcome to Policy Plus! Home editions do not come with the full set of policy definitions. Would you like to download them now? This can also be done later with Help | Acquire ADMX Files." and Yes opens the download window.

open: How does the service know whether the person's Windows edition has Group Policy support, now that it runs on a server rather than on the person's computer?

title: Use the downloaded definitions as the program's definitions
what: From the Help menu the person opens the download window and, after a successful download, the program discards what was loaded, loads the downloaded definitions, remembers them as the definitions to use and redraws its views.
why: So the new definitions are in use at once and are the ones the program starts with next time.

journey.name: Get definitions from the Help menu
steps: Choose Acquire ADMX Files
Run the download
Agree to open the new definitions
See the views rebuilt from them

criteria.says: Given the person chooses Acquire ADMX Files, when the download window closes with new definitions, then the loaded definitions and previous search results are discarded and the views are rebuilt from the downloaded ones; when it closes with no new definitions, then nothing has changed.
Given the downloaded definitions are loaded, when the program is next opened, then it uses them as the definitions, as a saved choice of the stored definitions rather than of a folder.
Given the program starts and the remembered definitions cannot be loaded, when it falls back, then it clears what was loaded and uses the default definitions instead of a chosen package.

Given the program starts and the place the person last chose to keep policy settings cannot be used, when it starts, then the person is told and the program goes back to its default place for policy settings.
Given the person picks a place to keep policy settings, when the choice is accepted, then the program remembers it for next time.
Given the person has not yet accepted the warning about editing policy files directly, when they accept it, then the program remembers that and does not show the warning again.
Given a policy file chosen as a source does not exist yet, when the program opens it, then a new empty file is created, so no policy in it is configured.

open: Where do the remembered choices of where policy settings are kept, and the policy file created when none exists, belong now that the program runs on a server?

title: Check and accept a new language for policy text
what: A person types the language code for policy text (such as en-US) and the product accepts it, refuses a code that is not in the form language-region, or does nothing when the code is unchanged.
why: Administrators read policy names and descriptions in their own language, so the product must take a code it can later use to find the matching template text.

terms.name: Policy text language
terms.means: The language code (for example en-US) that decides which language of template text is shown for policies; it is not the language of the product's own screens.

criteria.says: Given the language dialog is open, when the person confirms text that does not split into exactly two parts around one hyphen (for example "en" or "en-US-x"), then "Please enter a valid language code." is shown and the dialog stays open; any text with exactly one hyphen, including "-", "en-" or text with path characters, is accepted because it is not checked as a real language code, and the accepted text is later used as the name of the folder in which the template language files are looked for, so characters that do not belong in a folder name are not stopped here.

Given the language dialog shows the stored code, when the person confirms a code that, after its spaces are trimmed, is exactly equal to the stored code, which is compared as stored without trimming (upper and lower case count as different, so en-us differs from en-US), then the dialog closes as cancelled and nothing changes; otherwise the entered code, with its spaces trimmed, is returned as accepted, and saving it is done by another story.

open: The rule accepts any text with exactly one hyphen and the code becomes a folder name in the legacy product; should the new product keep accepting it, or refuse characters that do not belong in a language code?

title: Start Policy Plus with the last used definitions and sources
what: When a person opens the product it restores the policy definitions and the user and computer policy sources used last time, recovers with clear messages when either cannot be used, and shows the category tree ready to browse.
why: Administrators continue where they left off without choosing definitions and sources again, and are never left with a silent failure.

terms.name: Workspace
terms.means: The loaded policy definitions together with the open policy sources the person is working on; it is not a saved policy file.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: A place where the user or the computer policies are kept and read from; it is not the definitions that describe the policies.

terms.name: Definitions package
terms.means: The set of policy template files (ADMX and ADML) the workspace is loaded from, stored by the product; it is not a policy source.

terms.name: Default definitions package
terms.means: The definitions package loaded when none was saved or the saved one fails; it is the replacement for the definitions folder that Windows provides in the legacy product, not the person's own package.

terms.name: Starting source
terms.means: The policy source both sides open as when nothing usable was saved; in the legacy product it is the local Group Policy files, which the new product does not read from the person's computer.

journey.name: Open Policy Plus
steps: The person opens the product.
The product restores the saved policy sources and the saved definitions package.
If something cannot be used, the product says so and offers the default.
The person sees the category tree with both user and computer policies.

criteria.says: Given the product's settings are kept as one shared stored row of settings instead of in the Windows registry, when the product starts, then the saved policy sources, definitions package and policy text language are read from that row.

Given no policy sources were saved, when the product starts for the first time, then the user source and the computer source both open as the starting source with no extra location, because the service does not read the local Group Policy files of the person's computer.
Given a definitions package was saved last time, when the product starts, then that package is loaded from what the product stored; when none is saved, the default definitions package is loaded.

Given loading the saved definitions reports problems, when the person is asked whether to keep using the workspace, then Yes keeps the partly loaded workspace and No fails with "You decided to not use the problematic ADMX bundle.", which discards the workspace and is handled as a failed load: for a package that is not the default the person is asked to load the default, and for the default package the person is told the definitions could not be loaded.

Given the saved definitions package is not the default and fails to load, when the product starts, then the person is told that the definitions could not be loaded from the package, with the reason, and is asked "Load from the default location?"; Yes saves the default definitions package as the saved choice and No leaves the workspace empty with no further message.
Given the person chose to load the default location, when loading starts, then the workspace is replaced by an empty one and the default definitions package is loaded into it.

Given the default definitions package fails to load, or fails after the person chose Yes, when loading ends, then the person is told "Policy definitions could not be loaded: <reason>" and the workspace stays empty.

Given the previously saved policy sources cannot be opened, when the product starts, then the person is told "The previous policy sources are not accessible. The defaults will be loaded.", both sources are saved as the starting source and opened quietly, and only the kind of source is reset: any saved location text stays unchanged.

Given the policy sources dialog is opened with the last used sources, when it appears, then each side is set to the remembered kind (Local GPO, Registry, POL file, Scratch space, and for users also per-user GPO or user hive), and the registry path, file name, SID or hive path is filled in only for the kinds that carry one.

Given the service will later download Microsoft's policy definitions, when the product starts, then the secure connections it opens for that download allow only TLS 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 and no other protocol.
Given the workspace has loaded, when the category tree is first shown, then the area list stands on "User or Computer", so both user and computer policies are shown.

open: Which source replaces the local Group Policy files as the starting source on first start: an empty scratch space, or something the person uploads?
Which package is the default definitions package now that the definitions folder provided by Windows cannot be read: the package downloaded from Microsoft, or an uploaded one?
What does the person see when the stored settings cannot be read or written, given the legacy behaviour of silent defaults with nothing remembered no longer applies to the registry key?

The legacy product sets the allowed TLS versions when it starts, but the rule belongs to downloading Microsoft's definitions and no decision says whether TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are still allowed on the server; should it move to the story that downloads definitions, and which versions are wanted?

Which of the source kinds Local GPO, Registry, per-user GPO and user hive stay offered in the dialog, given that the live system sources are dropped and become imports, and what does their location text hold?

title: Show who made Policy Plus and which version this is
what: A person opens the About box to see the author, the project web address and, when known, the version of the product.
why: People can tell which build they are running and where to find the project.

journey.name: Check the version
steps: The person opens the About box from the menu.
The person reads the author, the project web address and the version if shown.

criteria.says: Given a person opens the About box, when it appears, then it names the author and the project web address, and adds the version only when a version was built into the product.

title: Change the language of policy text and reload
what: A person chooses the language of policy text, the product saves it at once and offers to reload the workspace so the new language applies.
why: Administrators see policy names and descriptions in the language they work in, without restarting.

journey.name: Switch policy text language
steps: The person opens the language choice from the menu.
The person enters a language code and confirms.
The product saves it and asks whether to reload the workspace.
The person chooses Yes and sees the policies in the new language.

criteria.says: Given the person confirmed a new language code, when it is accepted, then the code is saved at once in the shared stored settings and the person is asked "Language changes will take effect when ADML files are next loaded. Would you like to reload the workspace now?"; Yes empties the workspace and reloads the saved definitions package in that language.

title: Leave Policy Plus
what: A person chooses Exit and the product ends their use of it; the legacy product also cleaned up the open policy sources at that moment.
why: A person can finish their work and know the product is closed.

journey.name: Leave Policy Plus
steps: The person chooses Exit.
The product closes.

criteria.says: Given the product is open, when the person chooses Exit, then the product's screens end the person's use of it.
Given the service reads no folder, hive or Group Policy object of the person's computer, when the person leaves, then the service holds nothing open on their behalf and has no file to release.

open: What does Exit do in a web product: close the browser tab, return to a start screen, or something else?
Unsaved changes to a POL-backed source were lost without warning on leaving in the legacy product; should leaving now warn about them or keep them stored?

title: Look up a user's Group Policy object by account name
what: In the dialog for a user's Group Policy object, the person types an account name and presses Search to see its security identifier (SID), or types the SID directly, then confirms or cancels. The chosen SID names the object whose policy file is then imported by upload.
why: Administrators can point the user side of Policy Plus at one person's Group Policy object without knowing the SID by heart, and cannot go on with a SID that is not valid.

terms.name: Security identifier (SID)
terms.means: The identifier that names one account and its Group Policy object, such as S-1-5-21-...; it is not the account's display name.

terms.name: Per-user Group Policy object
terms.means: The policy kept for one named user account, used as the user policy source; it is not the local Group Policy that applies to everyone on the computer.

criteria.says: Given an account name is typed, when the person presses Search, then the account's SID appears in the SID box; and when the name cannot be translated, then the person is told "The name could not be translated to a SID."
Given a name is typed and the SID box is empty, when the person presses OK, then the name is looked up first, and the dialog stays open if no SID results.

Given the SID box holds text that is not a valid SID, when the person presses OK, then they are told "The SID is not valid. Enter a SID in the lower box, or enter a username in the top box and press Search to translate." and the dialog stays open; given a valid SID, then it is returned, the dialog closes as accepted and the person is asked to upload that object's policy file.
Given the dialog is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and nothing is chosen.

open: Which account names can Search translate to a SID now that no directory connection exists (decision 7 only replaces the lookup by a policy file upload), for example a fixed list, names in an uploaded file, or none so the SID is always typed?

title: Pick a user profile as the user policy source
what: In the user profile dialog, the person selects a profile folder and presses OK to use that profile's registry hive file (ntuser.dat) as the user policy source, or cancels with Escape. The hive's policies are brought in as an imported REG or POL file.
why: Administrators can edit the policies of a specific person's profile without being signed in as that person.

terms.name: User hive
terms.means: The file ntuser.dat in a profile folder, holding that person's registry settings; it is not the live registry of the signed-in person.

criteria.says: Given no profile is selected, when the person presses OK, then nothing happens; given a profile is selected, then that profile's hive is returned as the chosen user source, the dialog closes as accepted and the person is asked to import that hive's policies as a REG or POL file, since the live hive is not read.
Given the dialog is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and nothing is chosen.
