open: Where does the list of profile folders the person selects from come from, since the service reads no user folder (decision 1), and what stands in for the path C:\Users\<folder>\ntuser.dat that the legacy dialog returns?

title: Choose the computer policy source
what: In the policy sources dialog, the person chooses where the computer policies come from: the local Group Policy, a registry path, a POL file, or Scratch space. Each choice enables only its own box and Browse button, and the POL file is picked from the person's own machine.
why: The person can see which computer source is active and cannot type into one that is not chosen.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: The place where one side's policies are kept and saved back to: Local GPO, Registry, POL file, per-user GPO, user hive or Scratch space; it is not the template files that describe the policies.

terms.name: Scratch space
terms.means: An empty source that can be changed but is never saved anywhere; it is not a file the person can download.

criteria.says: Given the person selects a computer choice, when the dialog updates, then the registry path box is usable only with the Registry choice, and the POL file name box and its Browse button only with the POL file choice.

Given the person presses Browse for the computer POL file, when the file picker opens, then it accepts only '.pol' files, allows naming a file that does not exist yet, and does not ask before an existing file is chosen; the file comes from upload from the person's machine.

open: What is the content of the Local GPO choice, since decisions 1, 2 and 12 give no file-based replacement for the system's own policy folder: an uploaded Registry.pol, a stored copy, or is the choice not offered?

title: Choose the user policy source
what: In the policy sources dialog, the person chooses where the user policies come from: the local Group Policy, a registry path, a POL file, a per-user Group Policy object, a user hive, or Scratch space. Each choice enables only its own boxes and Browse buttons, which lead to the file picker and the two dialogs for a user's object or profile.
why: The person can set the user side separately from the computer side and cannot type into a box that does not belong to the chosen source.

criteria.says: Given the person selects a user choice, when the dialog updates, then the registry path box is usable only with Registry, the POL file box and Browse only with POL file, the SID box and Browse only with per-user GPO, and the hive path box and Browse only with user hive.

Given the person presses a Browse button for the user POL file, the user's Group Policy object or the user's profile, when the matching picker or dialog opens, then its result fills the box that belongs to that choice.

open: What is the content of the Local GPO choice on the user side, since decisions 1, 2 and 12 give no file-based replacement for the system's own policy folder?

title: Confirm or cancel the chosen policy sources
what: Pressing OK in the policy sources dialog creates the computer and user sources from the choices made, and keeps the dialog open with the reason when one cannot be created. Pressing Escape cancels.
why: The person only moves on with two working sources, and can back out without changing anything.

journey.name: Choose where policies are kept
steps: Open the policy sources dialog
Choose the computer source
Choose the user source
Press OK, or Escape to cancel

criteria.says: Given a computer choice, when the person presses OK, then the source is created from the choice (Local GPO, Registry with the typed path, POL file with the typed name, or Scratch space when none is chosen); if it cannot be created, then they are told "The computer policy loader could not be created." followed by the reason and the dialog stays open.

Given a user choice, when the person presses OK, then the source is created from the choice (Local GPO, Registry, POL file, per-user GPO with the typed SID, user hive with the typed file path, or Scratch space otherwise); if it cannot be created, then they are told "The user policy loader could not be created." followed by the reason and the dialog stays open; the dialog closes as accepted only when both sources were created.
Given the dialog is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled.

open: What does creating a Local GPO source from the choice mean in the target product, since no source of its content is stated?

title: Open the chosen policy sources
what: From the main screen, the person opens the policy sources dialog and, once accepted, the program opens the chosen user and computer sources and shows the result.
why: The person works on the policies of the source they chose, and sees at once whether it can be changed.

journey.name: Open policy sources
steps: Choose the open policy resources command
Choose the sources in the dialog
See the result of opening
Continue in the nearest visible category

criteria.says: Given the person accepted the policy sources dialog, when the sources are opened, then the opening result is shown and the view moves to the nearest visible category. Sources come from uploaded files and imports; the live system source is not offered.

title: Save policy changes to their sources
what: From the main screen, the person saves comments and policy settings back to the user and computer sources. Saved files are returned as downloads, including the policy file and gpt.ini of a Group Policy source. Nothing is written to a disk of the server's host, refreshed or applied live.
why: The person's work is kept in the file of the source it came from, with a clear outcome per side.

terms.name: gpt.ini
terms.means: The small file next to a Group Policy source's policy file that holds its version number and extension lines; it is not the policy file itself.

journey.name: Save policies
steps: Choose the save command
Comments are written for each source
Each writable source is saved
See the outcome for the user and computer sides

criteria.says: Given sources are open, when the person saves, then each source's comments are written first, then a source is written only if fully writable (otherwise reported "not writable"); the person sees "Success." with the user and computer outcomes, or "Saving failed!" with the reason.
Given a source has a comment list, when saving, then it is saved to its comment file location even when empty; a source without comment support has no list and is skipped.

Given comments are saved, when the file is written, then each comment gets its own text id built from the policy's namespace, policy name and a running number, and each distinct namespace gets a prefix made from its name (dots turned into underscores) and the running number.

Given comments are saved, when the file is written, then every comment and text held is written to the target file in schema version 1.0, replacing what the file held, and the file is offered as a CMTX download.

Given a local Group Policy source, when saved, then the Registry.pol and gpt.ini are produced with the version raised and offered as downloads, and the outcome tells that the files were produced for download; no policy refresh, Windows edition check or live registry difference is applied.

Given a per-user GPO source, when saved, then its Registry.pol is produced, its gpt.ini version is raised, both are offered as downloads, and the outcome tells that the files were produced for download; no policy refresh is invoked.

Given a POL file, registry, user hive or Scratch space source, when saved, then the outcome tells that the file was produced for download (POL file, registry and user hive sources, which are REG or POL files) or "discarded" (Scratch space); nothing is applied live and no change waits for a source to close.
Given a Group Policy source whose gpt.ini does not exist, when saved, then a new gpt.ini is written with the General section, both extension-name lines and Version 65537.
Given a gpt.ini exists, when updated, then its Version is raised by 1 for a machine source and by 65536 for a user source, and set to 65537 when no Version line exists.
Given a gpt.ini is updated, when the Machine and User extension-name lines for the registry policy are missing, then they are added; when present, they are left untouched.

open: What outcome wording replaces "saved to disk and invoked policy refresh", "saved to disk and applied diff to Registry", "already applied" and "will apply when policy source is closed", which describe disk writes, refreshes and live changes that decisions 1, 2 and 7 do not carry?

What is remembered for the next start (the legacy program keeps the chosen source types and locations), and for whom, since uploaded sources have no location on the server and decision 4 stores one shared settings row for all users?

title: Open a policy setting and see its current state
what: A person opens a policy and sees its name, help, support text, current state (Enabled, Disabled or Not configured), its comment and the section it applies to, and can switch between Enabled, Disabled, Not configured and between Computer and User.
why: Administrators need to see what a policy is set to, and for which section, before they change it.

terms.name: Policy setting
terms.means: The state of one policy (Enabled, Disabled or Not configured) with its option values and comment; not the policy's definition.

terms.name: Section
terms.means: Whether a policy setting is for the Computer or for the User; not a category of policies.

journey.name: Change a policy's setting
steps: Open a policy from the list
Read its current state, options and comment
Pick Enabled, Disabled or Not configured
Fill in the options
Press OK or Apply

criteria.says: Given a policy that names a supported-on text, when its dialog opens, then the Supported on box shows it, and the box is empty when the policy names none.

Given a policy for both Computer and User, when it opens without a section chosen, then it starts on Computer and the person can edit it for either; given a policy for one section, then the section is fixed and the choice is unavailable.
Given a policy whose stored state in the section is Enabled or Disabled, when the dialog opens, then that state is shown; for Not configured or an unclear state, Not Configured is shown.
Given the section being edited, when the dialog opens, then OK and Apply are available only when that section can be written to.
Given a section with no comments, when the dialog opens, then the comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable for this policy source"; otherwise it shows the stored comment or is empty.
Given the dialog is open, when Enabled is picked, then the option controls can be edited; when Disabled or Not Configured is picked, they are greyed out.

Given the person picks Computer or User, when the choice changes, then the writability, comments and chosen state reload from that section; option values are replaced only for options that section stores when Enabled, and other typed values stay.
Given extra width, when the dialog is resized, then the width is shared between the options panel and the help and comment boxes.
Given policy settings are stored by the service, when a section is chosen, then its state and comment come from the stored settings, not from the registry.

title: Enter list entries for a policy option
what: A person edits a list option in a grid and confirms it; entries are returned in order, and named lists refuse duplicate names.
why: List options such as allowed programs need entries the person can add, rename and check.

terms.name: List editor
terms.means: The grid in which a list option's entries are typed; not the policy dialog itself.

criteria.says: Given a list where the person names each entry, when two entries have exactly the same name and OK is pressed, then it is refused with "Multiple entries are named "<name>"! Remove or rename all but one." and nothing is returned; Run and run count as two entries.

Given a list without names, when OK is pressed, then every row except the empty new row at the bottom is returned in the order shown, even a row with an empty value; for named lists the new row is ignored.

open: What should happen when a name cell of a named list was never filled in? The old program stopped with an unhandled error.

title: Fill in a policy's option values
what: A person fills in a policy's options (numbers, text, choices, check boxes, lists), with each control starting from its default and limited by what the policy allows.
why: Every Enabled policy is only as useful as the option values the person can set correctly.

terms.name: Option
terms.means: One configurable value of a policy such as a number, text or choice; not the policy's state.

criteria.says: Given a check box option, when the dialog opens, then it starts with the presentation's default state.
Given a plain text option, when it is shown, then it is limited to the policy's maximum length and starts with the default text.
Given a number spin box, when it is shown, then it is limited to the policy's minimum and maximum, moves in the presentation's steps and starts at the default.
Given a drop-down, when it is shown, then the choices appear by translated name, sorted unless sorting is off, with the default preselected when one is named, otherwise nothing selected.
Given a text option with suggestions, when it is shown, then it is limited to the maximum length, starts with the default text and lists the suggestions, sorted unless sorting is off.

Given a plain number box, when text is entered, then text a whole-number reading accepts is kept (including sign or spaces), other text becomes the default, a number beyond the maximum or minimum becomes that limit, a number above 2,147,483,647 becomes the default, and a kept negative is converted to unsigned when applied; pasted text is not restricted.
Given a number box, when a key other than a digit or control key is typed, then it is ignored.

Given a policy that is Enabled in the section, when the dialog opens, then each option shows the stored value: numbers, text, the matching drop-down item, check box state, multi-line lines and the stored list.
Given a list option, when the person opens the list editor and confirms, then what it returns is kept as the option's value.

title: Apply option values to a policy and keep the dialog open
what: A person presses Apply to save the policy and its option values, each written in the form its definition asks for, while the dialog stays open.
why: Windows reads these stored values, so the form and the key must match the definition exactly.

terms.name: Apply
terms.means: Saving the policy and staying in the dialog; not closing it.

criteria.says: Given Apply, when pressed, then the policy is written, the dialog stays open and a change is recorded.
Given a setting that names its own key, when it is saved, then it goes under that key; otherwise under the policy's key.
Given a number option, when saved, then it is written as text if the definition says so, otherwise as a 32-bit number.
Given a text option, when saved, then it is an expandable string if the definition says so, otherwise a plain string.
Given a multi-line text option, when saved, then it is written as a multiple-string value.

Given a check box option, when saved, then a ticked box with no on value first saves 1 and an unticked box with no off value first removes the value, and the defined on or off value with its extra values then overwrites that.
Given a list option that does not keep other entries, when saved, then every existing value under its key is removed first and a list with no entries stays empty.

Given list entries, when saved, then entries carrying names use them; otherwise each is numbered from 1 and named with the definition's prefix plus the number, or by its own text when there is no prefix.
Given a choice option, when saved, then the chosen item's value and its extra values are written.

open: When the chosen choice position does not exist, the old program left the policy half set with no undo. Should the new product reject the save and write nothing instead?

title: Save a policy's state with OK
what: A person saves Enabled, Disabled or Not configured with options and comment by pressing OK, which closes the dialog.
why: This is the product's purpose: changing what a policy is set to.

criteria.says: Given a policy being saved, when OK or Apply is pressed, then everything the source holds for that policy is forgotten first, then the chosen state is written.
Given Not configured or Unknown, when saved, then nothing is written or removed beyond the forgetting, so the policy ends with no values.
Given Enabled is chosen, when applied, then every option is written whatever its value, including options never filled in.
Given Enabled and settings the person supplied, when written, then only supplied settings are written and unsupplied ones are left as they were.

Given Enabled, when saved, then the policy's own on value and its extra on values are saved, a blank list key falling back to the policy's key, and the number 1 when the policy has a value name but no on value.
Given a registry value to write for a policy, then a value defined as delete is removed, a number is saved as 32-bit, text as text, and a policy with no value writes nothing.
Given Disabled, when saved, then with no off value the registry value is removed, otherwise the off value and its extra off values are saved.

Given Disabled, when saved, then each setting gets only its own removal: lists lose all values under their key, check boxes with an off value or list get it saved, others lose their single value, and extra on values are left in place.
Given a source that supports comments, when applied, then an empty comment removes the stored comment and any text replaces or adds it.
Given OK, when pressed, then the policy is written and the dialog closes as a change.
Given the legacy registry and Group Policy sources, when saving, then the write goes to the stored policy settings for the section.

title: Close the policy setting dialog and report changes
what: Cancel and other ways of closing the dialog report whether a change was made.
why: The list behind the dialog refreshes only when a change was made, even if the person then cancels.

criteria.says: Given Apply was used earlier in the session, when Cancel is pressed, then the dialog closes reported as a change; otherwise as a cancel.
Given Apply was used earlier, when the dialog is closed by any other means, then it is still reported as a change.

title: Load a SPOL script into the import window
what: A person opens a SPOL file, edits its text, resets it, and leaves the window with Escape.
why: SPOL text is how settings move between machines; the person needs to prepare it before applying.

terms.name: SPOL
terms.means: Semantic policy text that lists policies with their state and options; not a registry file.

journey.name: Import settings from SPOL
steps: Open the import window
Open a SPOL file or type text
Verify it
Apply it
Read the result message

criteria.says: Given the person picks a SPOL file, when it is opened, then the whole file replaces the typed text without asking or checking; the file arrives by upload.
Given the import window opens, when it is shown, then any earlier parsed result is discarded so a cancelled session passes nothing back.
Given no text is selected, when Escape is pressed, then the window closes as cancelled; when text is selected, Escape closes nothing.
Given the text box, when Ctrl+A is pressed, then all text is selected.
Given the person confirms with Yes to "Are you sure you want to reset the text box?", when Reset is chosen, then the text becomes the header and blank lines.

title: Read, verify and apply SPOL text in the import window
what: A person verifies SPOL text to see how many settings it holds, or applies it, handing the parsed script back or being told it is invalid; the text is read line by line into policy states and settings.
why: People should see mistakes before anything changes.

criteria.says: Given SPOL text, when read, then it must begin with the signature line "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" or is refused with "Incorrect signature.".
Given SPOL text, when read, then lines are split at carriage return and line feed, so line-feed-only text is read as one line and refused with the signature message.

Given a policy header, when read, then it is a user policy only when its first word is exactly U, otherwise machine; the rest is the identifier; a header without a space fails with the line number and no reason.
Given a policy state, when read, then it must be Not configured, Enabled or Disabled in any letter case, otherwise refused with "Unknown policy state.".
Given an Enabled policy, when read, then its settings are read; lines under Not configured or Disabled are read as the next header.

Given a setting value, when read, then # starts a whole number (failing with a conversion message), a plain non-negative number is unsigned, True or False in any case is yes/no, single quotes are text, double quotes a list, None an empty list, anything else "Unknown option data format.".

Given a bracketed setting, when read, then one-text lines make a list and two-text lines a name and value table; with no entries a list setting loses its existing entries unless the definition keeps them, and any other kind fails to write.
Given comment lines, when read, then they are recognised in any letter case, with a double backslash read as one backslash and backslash n as a line break.
Given a comment ending in a lone backslash or with an unknown escape, when read, then it is refused with "Escape sequence started at end of comment." or "Unknown comment escape sequence" naming it.
Given a failure while reading, then the message ends with "(Error found on line N.)".
Given SPOL text, when Verify is pressed, then it reports "Validation successful, N policy settings found." or "SPOL validation failed: " and the reason, and nothing is applied.
Given SPOL text, when Apply is pressed, then valid text is passed back to the main window; invalid text is refused with "The SPOL text is invalid: " and the reason.

title: Inspect and copy a SPOL fragment
what: A person sees the SPOL text of a fragment, can show or hide the header line, select all and copy it.
why: Administrators move single settings between machines by copying their SPOL text.

criteria.says: Given the fragment window opens, when it is shown, then the text is focused and fully selected.
Given Include SPOL header, when ticked, then the text starts with the heading and a blank line; otherwise only the fragment shows.
Given the text box, when Ctrl+A is pressed, then all text is selected.
Given the text, when Copy is pressed, then the whole text is selected and copied to the clipboard.

title: Import a semantic policy into the stored settings
what: A person imports SPOL text and its policies are applied to the computer and user settings and their comments, with a result message.
why: One import sets many policies at once.

criteria.says: Given parsed SPOL, when applied, then each policy goes to the machine or user source by its section.
Given a policy with a comment and a comment store, when applied, then the comment is stored first; an empty comment leaves any existing one alone.
Given a policy, when applied, then its earlier settings are wiped and then the stated state and settings are written.
Given many policies, when one fails, then it is skipped and counted and the rest are applied; only the failure count is reported.
Given the import finishes, then the person sees "Semantic Policy successfully applied." or "N out of M could not be applied." and the view refreshes either way.

open: If writing a policy fails, the old program kept the new comment against a half-written policy. Should the new product keep the comment or undo it?
Should the failure message say which policies failed and why? The old one gave only a count.

title: Ignore double-clicks on product ticks in the filter
what: Double-clicking a product's checkbox in the filter's product list does nothing, so the tick a person sees is always the tick that is kept.
why: Administrators build product filters quickly and must be able to trust what is ticked.

criteria.says: Given the product list in the filter dialog, when a person double-clicks a product's checkbox, then nothing changes and the tick shown is the tick kept.

terms.name: Supported on
terms.means: The filter condition that keeps policies supported by the chosen products; it is not the Policy type or Current state condition.

terms.name: Product requirement box
terms.means: The part of the filter dialog holding the product list and the two matching options; it is not the whole dialog.

title: Choose the products a filter requires
what: In the filter dialog a person ticks Supported on to use the product requirement box, and ticks products, each tick spreading to the products beneath it.
why: Administrators narrow the policy list to the policies that apply to the Windows versions and products they manage.

criteria.says: Given the filter dialog has just opened, when Supported on is not ticked, then the product list and the two matching options cannot be used; when it is ticked they can be used.
Given Supported on is ticked, when a person ticks or unticks a product by hand, then every product beneath it is ticked or unticked to match, and changes the dialog makes itself do not spread.
Given Supported on is not ticked, when the dialog shows the product list, then the list looks unusable and readable.

terms.name: Filter
terms.means: The set of conditions on type, state, comment and supported products that a policy must meet to be listed; it is not a search.

title: Apply the options chosen in the filter dialog
what: Pressing OK in the filter dialog builds a filter from the chosen type, state, comment and supported-on options and closes the dialog accepted.
why: Administrators see only the policies that meet their conditions.

criteria.says: Given a Policy type is chosen, when OK is pressed, then the filter keeps only managed policies for Policy, only unmanaged ones for Preference, and has no policy-type condition for Any.
Given a Current state is chosen, when OK is pressed, then the filter requires Not Configured, Configured, Enabled or Disabled as chosen, and Any sets no state condition.
Given a Commented choice, when OK is pressed, then the filter keeps only commented policies for Yes, only uncommented ones for No, and has no comment condition for Any.

Given Supported on is ticked, when OK is pressed, then the filter records every ticked product and both matching options, and is accepted even when no product is ticked; given it is unticked, any ticks and options are discarded and no support condition applies.

title: Open, reset or cancel the filter dialog
what: The filter dialog opens showing the filter now in force; a person can reset every choice to its default, or press Escape to close it without changing the current filter.
why: People can start over or back out without side effects.

criteria.says: Given the current filter has no policy-type condition, or keeps only managed policies, or only the others, when the dialog opens, then Policy type shows Any, Policy or Preference respectively.
Given the current filter has no state condition, or requires Not Configured, Configured, Enabled or Disabled, when the dialog opens, then Current state shows Any or that state.
Given the current filter has no comment condition, or keeps only commented, or only uncommented policies, when the dialog opens, then Commented shows Any, Yes or No respectively.

Given the current filter has a supported-on condition, when the dialog opens, then Supported on is ticked, exactly the filter's products are ticked, both matching options are set as the filter holds, and product branches whose tick differs from their parent are opened.

Given the current filter has no supported-on condition, when the dialog opens, then Supported on is unticked, both "Match a policy if at least one selected product is supported" and "Match policies with missing or blank support definitions" are ticked, and no product is ticked.

Given any choices in the filter dialog, when Reset is pressed, then Policy type, Current state and Commented return to Any, Supported on is unticked, both matching options are ticked and no product is ticked.
Given the filter dialog is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes as cancelled and the current filter is unchanged.

title: Turn the filter on and change it from the main window
what: From the main window a person opens the filter dialog, which turns "Only Filtered Policies" on when changed, and switches the filter on or off with that menu entry.
why: Administrators can narrow the policy lists and widen them again at will.

journey.name: Narrow the list with a filter
steps: Open the filter options from the menu
Choose conditions and press OK
See only the filtered policies and the nearest visible category
Switch Only Filtered Policies off to see everything again

criteria.says: Given the filter dialog is accepted, when the filter options change, then "Only Filtered Policies" turns on and the view moves to the nearest visible category.
Given the main window, when a person chooses "Only Filtered Policies", then the filter switches on or off and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

terms.name: Find by ID
terms.means: The lookup of one item by its identifier; it is not a text search.

title: Look up an identifier as it is typed
what: Typing an ID in Find by ID looks it up as a category, product, support definition or policy and shows what was found, with the section a policy ID names.
why: Administrators who know an ID reach the exact item without browsing.

criteria.says: Given text typed in Find by ID, when it is trimmed and looked up, then a category is tried first, then a product, then a support definition, then a policy; the first kind that matches is selected with its own icon, and a policy is looked up only when no other kind matches.

Given the text matches nothing, when it is typed, then nothing is selected and a "not found" icon is shown; given the text is empty, a blank icon is shown; and a section from an earlier match is not cleared when the text changes to a non-policy.
Given a policy ID, when it ends with "@U" or "@C", then it means the user or computer section; with no suffix or any other suffix it applies to both, and the suffix is cut off before the lookup.
Given Find by ID opens, then the status icons come from the product's icon set and the ID box is focused and empty.

title: Confirm Find by ID and limit the area and selection choices
what: Go accepts Find by ID with the typed ID whether or not it matched, Escape closes it as cancelled, and the area choice, policy selection and menu offer only supported options.
why: People decide when to go to what they found, or give up.

criteria.says: Given Find by ID is open, when Go is pressed, then it closes accepted with the typed text, even when nothing matched, so the caller may receive no selection.
Given Find by ID is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes as cancelled.
Given the area choice, when a person opens it, then it offers only "User or Computer", "User" and "Computer" and accepts no typed text.
Given the policy list, when a person selects a policy, then only that one is selected.
Given the main menu, when a person looks for Deduplicate Policies, then it is not offered.

open: Should a policy hidden by the area choice or the filter still leave the category shown with no message, or should the person be told why nothing is selected?
title: Go to a policy, category, product or support definition by ID
what: From the main window a person enters an ID and the product moves to the matching category or policy, or opens the product or support details.
why: Administrators jump straight to a known item.

journey.name: Jump to an item by its ID
steps: Choose Find by ID from the menu
Type the ID and press Go
Land on the category, policy editor or details of the item

criteria.says: Given an ID is accepted, when it names a visible category, a policy, a product, a support definition or nothing known, then the category opens, the policy opens in the editor with the list moved to it, the product or support details open, or "That object could not be found." is shown; a hidden category shows "The category is not currently visible. Change the view settings and try again."

Given a policy is found, when the list moves to it, then its category is shown only when visible in the tree, the policy row is selected only if listed there, and a policy hidden by the area or the filter leaves the category shown with nothing selected and no message.
Given a policy found by ID, when it opens, then the area is the lower-numbered of the area shown and the area found, so Computer wins over User.

title: Refuse unusable text searches and cancel with Escape
what: Find by text refuses an empty search or one with no attribute ticked, and closes as cancelled on Escape.
why: People get a clear reason instead of an empty result.

criteria.says: Given Find by text is open with empty search text, when Search is pressed, then the search is refused with "Please enter search terms."

Given In title, In description and In comment all start ticked, when none is ticked and Search is pressed, then the search is refused with "At least one attribute must be searched. Check one of the boxes and try again."
Given Find by text is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes as cancelled.

terms.name: Wildcard word
terms.means: A search word containing * or ? that matches any run or any one character; it is not a plain word.

terms.name: Hit
terms.means: A policy that meets the search; it is not a policy merely listed.

open: Should an unclosed quote still be dropped silently, as today, or should the person be told?
Decision 6 says no comment search is carried, yet the rule matches comments from the user and computer sources; should In comment be searched or dropped?
title: Find policies by title, description or comment text
what: Search text is split into words, wildcards and phrases, and matches policies whose title, description or comment hit every word, wildcard and phrase of the search text.
why: Administrators locate policies by what they remember of their wording.

criteria.says: Given search text, when it is split, then plain words, wildcard words (with "*" or "?") and quoted phrases are told apart, and words are lowercased, trimmed and lose the characters . , ' " ; / ! ( ) { } [ ].

Given a phrase opened with a double quote, when a later word ends in a double quote, then the phrase runs between them; a phrase never closed is dropped without telling the person, widening the search, and a single quoted word such as "abc" does not close itself so it absorbs the following words.

Given parsed search text, when a text is tested, then it is a hit only if it contains every plain word as a whole word, every wildcard matches some word, and every quoted phrase appears as whole words together.
Given the ticked attributes, when a policy's title or description hits, then the policy matches; any one hit is enough.

title: Refuse unusable registry searches and cancel with Escape
what: Find by registry refuses empty terms and terms that name a root key, and closes as cancelled on Escape.
why: People are told how to fix their terms.

criteria.says: Given both key and value are empty, when Search is pressed, then the search is refused with "Please enter search terms."

Given key text starts with a root key name for the local machine or the current user, short or full, followed by a backslash, when Search is pressed, then it is refused with "Policies' root keys are determined only by their section. Remove the root key from the search terms and try again."
Given Find by registry is open, when Escape is pressed, then it closes as cancelled.

title: Find policies by registry key and value
what: Search matches policies that read or write a registry value meeting every key and value term entered.
why: Administrators who know a registry location find the policy that controls it.

criteria.says: Given terms entered, when a policy is tested, then it matches when at least one registry value it reads or writes meets every term, ignoring case.
Given a value-name term, when it is matched, then the whole name must match, with "*" and "?" as wildcards, otherwise equal.
Given a key term with no backslash and no wildcard, then it matches policies with a key path part equal to it.
Given a key term with a backslash and no wildcard, then it matches policies whose key path starts with that text.
Given a key term with "*" or "?", then it must match the whole key path as a wildcard pattern.

title: Search every policy and list the hits as they are found
what: The results window tests every policy in turn, adds each hit with its category, and refreshes its list and progress as it goes.
why: Administrators see results early on a long search.

criteria.says: Given a search is waiting, when the results window is shown, then the search tests every policy in turn and adds each hit to the list with its category name, in the order policies are held.
Given a running search, when 20 more policies are checked, then the list and progress refresh with "Searching: checked N policies so far, found M hits".
Given the results list, when the window is resized or shown, then the title column fills the list width and drawing is smooth.

title: Report how a search ended and let the person stop it
what: Stop or closing the window cancels a search, and the window reports how the search ended.
why: People can abandon a long search and know what was covered.

criteria.says: Given a search ends, when it finishes or is stopped, then it reports "Finished searching: checked N policies, found M hits" or "Search canceled: ..." and Stop is disabled.
Given a running search, when Stop is pressed or the window is closed, then the search is cancelled; closing before it finishes leaves "Search canceled" with the bar full.

terms.name: Search results
terms.means: The policies a search found, kept so the person can return to them; it is not the filter.

title: Choose a search result and reopen the results
what: Go or a double-click takes the selected result, and reopening the window selects the earlier result again.
why: People continue from where they left off.

criteria.says: Given a result is selected, when Go or a double-click is used, then the window accepts, passes the policy back and remembers its position; with none selected it does not accept.
Given the window is reopened, when the earlier selected result is still listed, then it is selected again.

title: Start a text or registry search from the main window
what: The main window starts a search from the text or registry dialog's terms, clears earlier results and opens the picked policy.
why: Administrators move from a search to the policy in one flow.

journey.name: Search for a policy
steps: Choose Find by text or by registry
Enter terms and press Search
Watch results appear
Pick a result and edit the policy

criteria.says: Given Find by text, when terms are entered, then a search starts with them and can search both areas' comments.
Given Find by registry, when terms are entered, then a search starts with them.
Given a search starts, then earlier results are cleared, the progress range is the number of policies and it begins on "Starting search".
Given a search dialog opens empty or runs a new search, when a result is picked, then its editor opens in the current area and the list moves to that policy.

title: Reopen the last search results
what: "Search Results" shows the last results again without a new search.
why: People revisit results after editing a policy.

criteria.says: Given a search was run, when "Search Results" is chosen, then the last results reopen and no new search starts.
Given no search has been run or it was cleared, when it is chosen, then "No search has been run yet, so there are no results to display." is shown and nothing opens.

title: Step to the next search result
what: Find Next moves to the next visible policy in the results.
why: Administrators work through hits one by one.

criteria.says: Given results, when Find Next is chosen, then it moves to the next currently visible result, skipping hidden ones, and shows "There are no more results that match the filter." when none is left.
Given no search has run or the last result has been passed, when the next policy is taken, then nothing is returned; otherwise it is the result after the last chosen one.

title: Choose whether to work on user or computer policies
what: A small choice window asks which area, User or Computer, the person wants to work on, and offers only the areas the task allows.
why: Importing, exporting and raw editing all act on one area at a time, so the person must say which one before anything changes.

terms.name: Area
terms.means: One of the two halves of policy settings, User policies or Computer policies; not a single policy and not a file.

criteria.says: Given the choice window is open, when the person presses OK before choosing User or Computer, then nothing happens; once one is chosen, OK reports that area to the task that asked and closes the window as accepted.
Given the choice window is open, when the person presses Escape, then the window closes as cancelled and no area is chosen.

title: See and select the keys and values of a policy file
what: The raw editor lists every key of the uploaded policy file with its sub-keys and values, shows special deletion entries as such, and offers only the buttons that fit what is selected.
why: Administrators who edit a policy file directly need to see exactly what it holds and be stopped from actions that make no sense for the selected item.

terms.name: Policy file
terms.means: The file of raw registry-style keys and values that holds policy settings for one area; not the policy definitions that describe them.

terms.name: Deletion entry
terms.means: A special entry in a policy file that tells the machine to remove a value or all values when policies are applied; not an ordinary value.

journey.name: Review a policy file in the raw editor
steps: The person opens the raw editor on an uploaded policy file.
They read the list of keys, sub-keys and values.
They select a key or a value and see which actions are available.

criteria.says: Given a policy file with several keys, when the editor opens, then keys are listed in alphabetical order ignoring case, each followed by its indented sub-keys and then its values in alphabetical order, and a value with an empty name (the marker that keeps an empty key) is not listed.
Given a key name appears more than once with different letter case, when sub-keys are listed, then it appears only once and the key being listed is never listed as its own sub-key.

Given ordinary values of several kinds, when they are listed, then a list of text shows its items joined by spaces, text shows as it is, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers show in decimal, binary data shows as hexadecimal bytes separated by spaces, and other kinds show no content.

Given special deletion entries, when they are listed, then the delete-values entry shows as "Delete values" with its data, an entry that deletes one value shows as "Delete value" with the name, and entries that clear everything show as "Delete all values"; none of them can be edited or deleted.
Given nothing is selected in the list, when the person looks at the buttons, then only Add key and Export are available and Add value, Delete value, Edit and Forget are unavailable.
Given a key is selected, when the person looks at the buttons, then Add key, Add value, Delete value, Forget and Export are available and Edit is unavailable.

Given a value is selected, when the person looks at the buttons, then Forget is always available, Add key, Add value and Export are unavailable, and Edit and Delete value are available only when the value is not already a deletion entry.

title: Close the raw editor with Done or Escape
what: Done and Escape both close the raw editor; Done closes it as accepted and Escape as cancelled, and there is no Cancel button.
why: Every change is applied to the loaded policy file as it is made, so closing never undoes anything and the person must know that.

criteria.says: Given the raw editor is open with changes already made, when the person presses Done or Enter the editor closes as accepted, and when they press Escape it closes as cancelled; either way every change stays applied to the loaded policy file, to be saved to the stored file only when policies are saved.

title: Add a key to a policy file
what: The person types a new key name, and an empty key of that name is added under the selected key, or at the top level when nothing is selected.
why: Administrators need to create keys that policy definitions will later fill.

terms.name: Key
terms.means: A named folder in a policy file that holds values and sub-keys; not a value.

journey.name: Add a key
steps: The person selects a parent key, or nothing for the top level.
They press Add key and type a name.
The new key appears in the list, selected.

criteria.says: Given the key name window is confirmed, when the name was typed, then the typed name is handed over unchecked; when it is cancelled, an empty name is handed over, so cancelling and typing nothing look the same.
Given the typed name contains a backslash, when the person confirms, then they are told "The key name is not valid." and no key is added.
Given a key of the same name, ignoring case, already exists under the same parent, when the person confirms, then they are told "The key name is already taken." and no key is added.

Given the name is empty or the window was cancelled, when the person adds a key, then nothing is added; otherwise, given a valid free name, an empty key of that name is created under the selected key, or at the top level when nothing is selected, and it is selected in the list.

title: Add a value to the selected key
what: The person chooses a value name and one of five kinds, then enters its data, and the value is stored under the selected key.
why: Administrators need to write a raw value that no policy definition covers.

terms.name: Value
terms.means: A named piece of data of one kind stored under a key in a policy file; not a key and not a policy.

criteria.says: Given the new value window opens, when the person looks at it, then String, Expandable string, List of strings, 32-bit DWord and 64-bit QWord are offered with String chosen; confirming hands over the typed name unchecked, possibly empty, with the chosen kind, and cancelling hands over neither.

Given a name and kind are chosen, when the data window opens, then its starting data is empty text, zero, or an empty list by kind; if the person then confirms the data, the value is stored under the selected key and replaces without warning any value of the same name there, and if they do not confirm, nothing is stored.

title: Edit the data of a value
what: The person changes the data of the selected value in a text, number or list-of-text window that fits its kind.
why: Administrators correct raw values without recreating them.

criteria.says: Given a value is selected, when the person edits it, then a plain or expandable text value opens a text box, a 32-bit or 64-bit number a number box and a list of text a multi-line box; any other kind, such as binary, is refused with "This value kind is not supported." and nothing changes; cancelling leaves the value as it was.
Given the number box is open, when the person types a number, then a 32-bit value accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295 and a 64-bit value accepts 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615.
Given the person confirms new data, when it is stored, then the value keeps its name and kind, its data is replaced and it stays selected.

title: Mark a value for deletion or clear a key
what: From the selected item, the person marks a value for deletion, or clears a key either completely, keeping its direct values, or by deleting one named value.
why: A policy file can tell a machine to remove settings when policies are applied, so administrators must be able to record that intent.

terms.name: Cleared key
terms.means: A key marked so that applying policies removes the values the machine holds in it; not a key forgotten from the file.

criteria.says: Given a value is selected and not already a deletion entry, when the person deletes it, then the value is not erased from the file but replaced by a deletion entry named after it, which removes the value on the machine when policies are applied.

Given a key is selected, when the person deletes it, then three choices are offered and OK does nothing until one is chosen; cancelling or Escape changes nothing. Clear everything removes all values and marks the key cleared; Clear first marks it cleared and puts back only its existing direct values with ordinary content, losing deletion entries already in the key and not putting back values of sub-keys; Delete one value is refused with "You must enter a value name." when the name is empty, and otherwise removes any value of that name, whether or not it exists, and replaces it with a deletion entry.

title: Choose how to delete a key in the delete window
what: A window lets the person pick one of three ways to delete, and asks for a value name only when deleting one value.
why: The choice must be clear before a key is changed, and a missing value name must be caught early.

criteria.says: Given the delete window has just opened, when the person looks at it, then no option is chosen and pressing Delete with none chosen does nothing; choosing the option to clear the key or to delete all values under it and pressing Delete accepts the choice without further input.

Given the option to delete one value is chosen, when the value name is empty and the person presses Delete, then they are told "You must enter a value name." and the window stays open; with a name, the choice is accepted.
Given the options are shown, when the option to delete one value is not chosen, then the value name box cannot be typed in; when it is chosen, it can.
Given the delete window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and nothing changes.

title: Forget a key or a value without leaving a deletion mark
what: The person removes a key with everything in it, or one value, from the policy file entirely, after confirming.
why: Sometimes the file should say nothing at all about a setting, rather than tell the machine to delete it.

terms.name: Forget
terms.means: To remove an entry from the policy file leaving no deletion mark; not the same as deleting, which leaves a mark.

criteria.says: Given a key is selected, when the person chooses Forget, then they are asked "Are you sure you want to remove this key and all its contents?"; on Yes the key, all its sub-keys, every value and every clearing mark are removed with no deletion entry left, and No changes nothing; forgetting a selected value removes the value and its deletion entry the same way.

title: Start a registry file import from the raw editor
what: The Import button in the raw editor opens the registry file import window and refreshes the list when values were imported.
why: Administrators can bring registry export files into the policy file they are editing without leaving the editor.

criteria.says: Given the raw editor is open, when the person presses Import, then the registry file import window opens.
Given the import window reports that values were imported, when it closes, then the list of keys and values is rebuilt to show them; otherwise it is left as it was.

title: Start a registry file export of the selected key
what: The Export button opens the registry file export window with the selected key as its starting branch and the right registry prefix.
why: Administrators can take one branch, or the whole policy file, out as a registry file.

terms.name: Registry prefix
terms.means: The text put in front of key names in a registry file, such as the current-user or local-machine prefix; not part of the key's name in the policy file.

terms.name: Source branch
terms.means: The key whose contents are exported, with everything below it; empty means the whole policy file.

criteria.says: Given a key is selected, when the export window opens, then the source branch starts as that key, or empty with nothing selected; the person can type over it, the export uses the text in the box at the time, and an empty box exports all of the policy file.

Given the user policy file is being edited, when the export window opens, then the prefix box starts as the current-user prefix, and as the local-machine prefix for the computer policy file; it can be changed and the export uses the text in the box unchecked.

title: Name a new key in the key name window
what: The key name window puts the cursor in the name box with its text selected, and Escape closes it as cancelled.
why: The person can type a name straight away or back out without a mouse.

criteria.says: Given the key name window appears, when it is shown, then the cursor is in the name box and any text in it is selected.
Given the key name window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and no key is added.

title: Cancel the list-of-text window with Escape
what: Pressing Escape in the window that edits a list of text closes it as cancelled.
why: A person can leave the edit without changing the value.

criteria.says: Given the list-of-text window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and the value is unchanged.

title: Switch the number box between decimal and hexadecimal
what: In the number window the person can show the number in decimal or hexadecimal, and Escape closes it as cancelled.
why: Registry numbers are often written in hexadecimal, so the person can read and type in either form.

criteria.says: Given the number window shows a number, when the person ticks or unticks Hexadecimal, then the same number is displayed in hexadecimal or decimal.
Given the number window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and the value is unchanged.

title: Cancel the text window with Escape
what: Pressing Escape in the window that edits text closes it as cancelled.
why: A person can leave the edit without changing the value.

criteria.says: Given the text window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and the value is unchanged.

title: Cancel the new value window with Escape
what: Pressing Escape in the window that asks for a value name and kind closes it as cancelled.
why: A person can leave without adding a value.

criteria.says: Given the new value window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and no value is added.

title: Choose the file for a registry export
what: In the export window the person picks the name of the registry file to write, or cancels with Escape.
why: The person needs to say where the exported registry file goes, or leave without exporting.

criteria.says: Given the export window is open, when the person chooses a file name, then it is shown in the file box; in the web product the file is delivered as a download rather than written to a folder.
Given the export window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and nothing is exported.

open: Does the person still type a file name in the web product, or is the download named automatically?

title: Export a branch of a policy file as a registry file
what: The person writes the chosen branch of the policy file out as a registry file.
why: Registry files can be reviewed, shared, and imported on machines that use the built-in registry editor.

terms.name: Registry file
terms.means: A text file of registry keys and values that Windows can import; not a policy file.

criteria.says: Given no file name was given, when the person presses Export, then they are told "Please specify a filename and path for the exported REG." and nothing is written.
Given the policy file is applied to the export, when the export is built, then the whole file is applied as the difference from an empty file, so nothing is forgotten.
Given a source branch ends with a backslash, when the export is built, then the trailing backslash is removed before the branch is used.
Given keys are marked for removal and values for deletion, when the registry file is written, then a removed key is written with a leading minus sign and a deleted value as a bare minus sign.

Given values of every kind, when the registry file is written, then a default value is shown as an at sign, quotes and backslashes in names and text are escaped, text is quoted, a 32-bit number is "dword:" with eight hexadecimal digits, and every other kind including 64-bit numbers, expandable text and multiple strings is written as hex bytes with its type number as hex(n), except plain binary which is hex; lines wrap before column 78 with a trailing backslash.

Given the file is written, when the export succeeds, then the person is told "REG exported successfully." and the window closes; on any failure they are told only "Failed to export REG!" and the window stays open.

title: Choose a registry file to import and guess its prefix
what: The person picks a registry file, and the program guesses the key prefix from it and warns about default values.
why: Registry files name keys in full, and the program must know how much of the name to strip to place them in a policy file.

terms.name: Default value
terms.means: The value of a registry key that has no name, written as an at sign in a registry file; not a value called default.

criteria.says: Given the person browses for a registry file, when the chooser opens, then only files of type *.reg are offered; in the web product the file is uploaded.

Given a file is chosen and the prefix is empty, when the file is read, then the prefix is guessed from it, and if the file holds default values the person is warned "This REG file contains data for default values, which cannot be applied to all policy sources."

Given the file's first key belongs to the users hive, when the prefix is guessed, then it is that hive plus the user identifier; for any other first key, including the current-user hive, it is the hive name alone; a first key with no further backslash gives an empty prefix; a file with no keys gets the local-machine prefix.
Given any value in the file has an empty name, when the file is read, then it is reported as holding default values.
Given the guess fails, when the file is read, then the person is only warned "An error occurred while trying to guess the prefix." and the prefix stays empty.

title: Import a registry file into a policy file
what: The person loads a registry file with its prefix and applies it to the policy file.
why: Settings exported from another machine or tool can be brought into the policy file in one step.

criteria.says: Given no file is named, when the person presses Import, then they are told "Please specify a REG file to import." and nothing is imported; with no prefix they are told "Please specify the prefix used to fully qualify paths in the REG file."
Given the first line is not "Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00", when the file is read, then it is refused with "Incorrect REG signature".
Given blank lines and lines starting with a semicolon, when the file is read, then they are ignored.
Given a key header, when it starts with a minus sign, then the whole key is marked for removal; otherwise it opens a key whose values follow.
Given a value line starting with an at sign, when the file is read, then it is the key's default value with an empty name.

Given value data, when it is read, then a bare minus sign is a value to delete, quoted data is text, "dword:" is a 32-bit number in hexadecimal, and "hex" is bytes typed by the number in brackets or binary if none; data in none of these forms is kept as a value with no data and no type, with no error.
Given a key name, when it starts with the prefix regardless of case, then the prefix is removed; a key not starting with it keeps its full original name.
Given the file is read, when it is applied, then a key marked for removal is cleared, a value marked for deletion is deleted, any other value is saved, and the source branch limit is not checked.

Given the file is loaded and applied straight to the chosen policy file, when it succeeds, then the policy file holds the imported entries; on any failure the person is told only "Failed to import the REG file."

open: What should happen when a key does not start with the prefix: should the web product apply the full original name as the old program did, or refuse it?
What should the person see for data in an unrecognised form: an empty value written, or a refusal?

title: Cancel the registry import with Escape
what: Pressing Escape in the registry import window closes it as cancelled.
why: A person can leave without importing.

criteria.says: Given the import window is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled and nothing is imported.

title: Import a POL file into the user or computer policies
what: The person picks a POL file and an area, and the file's settings are applied to that area's policy file.
why: Policy files made elsewhere, for example copied from a domain, can be brought into the product.

terms.name: POL file
terms.means: A Windows policy file that stores raw registry-style policy settings for one area; not a registry export file.

journey.name: Import a POL file
steps: The person chooses Import POL and picks a file to upload.
They choose User or Computer.
They see whether the import worked.

criteria.says: Given the area choice is shown, when the person looks at it, then User and Computer are each usable only when the task allows that area.

Given a POL file is chosen by upload and an area is chosen, when it can be read, then it is applied to that area and the person is told "POL import successful." with nothing saved for good until the person saves; when it cannot be read they are told "The POL file could not be loaded." and nothing changes.

title: Export a policy area as a POL file
what: The person writes an area's policy settings out as a POL file download.
why: A POL file can be copied to a machine or domain that applies it.

criteria.says: Given an area is chosen, when the person exports, then a policy file held by the product is used as is, and policy state that came from imported registry files is rebuilt as a new POL file from the three policy locations.

Given a POL file is rebuilt from registry files, when it is built, then every value and every sub-key under each of the three policy locations is copied with its own data type and environment variables left unexpanded.
Given the export is done, when it succeeds, then the person is told "POL exported successfully."; if it cannot be saved, they are told "The POL file could not be saved."

open: The old program stopped with an unhandled error when one of the three policy locations was missing; what should the person see instead?

title: Open the raw editor on a policy file after a warning
what: From the main screen the person opens the raw editor on a policy file, after accepting a caution the first time.
why: Raw editing can leave policies inconsistent, so the person must knowingly accept the risk, and only a policy file that can be edited directly is offered.

criteria.says: Given neither area is backed by an uploaded policy file, when the person chooses to edit the raw policy file, then they are told "Neither loaded source is backed by a POL file."; the area they may choose is limited to areas backed by a policy file.

Given the person has never accepted the caution, when they open the raw editor, then they must accept "Caution! This tool is for very advanced users. Improper modifications may result in inconsistencies in policies' states."; Yes continues and records the acceptance, and No cancels and asks again next time.

open: Where is the acceptance of the caution remembered in the web product: per browser, or in the shared settings?

title: Export a policy area as a registry file from the main screen
what: The person chooses an area and the registry file export window opens for that area's policy file.
why: Settings can be handed to Windows' own registry import.

criteria.says: Given the person chooses an area, when they export to a registry file, then the area's policy settings, as a POL, are handed to the export window; if they cannot be produced, the person is told what went wrong.

open: The old program stopped with an unhandled error for an unsupported source, unlike Export POL, which told the person; should the web product tell the person here too?

title: Import a registry file from the main screen
what: The person chooses an area and imports a registry file into its policy file, and the view refreshes.
why: Settings from registry files show up as policy states without a separate step.

criteria.says: Given the person chooses an area and imports a registry file, when the import succeeds, then the file is applied to that area's policy file and the view is refreshed to show the new policy states.

title: Enter whole numbers in hexadecimal when editing a number value
what: When someone edits a number value in a policy file, they can switch the number field to hexadecimal, see the value as hexadecimal text, and type a hexadecimal number to set it.
why: Administrators often know registry numbers in hexadecimal and the values can be larger than the ordinary number field can handle; typing them as they know them avoids conversion mistakes.

terms.name: Hexadecimal mode
terms.means: The setting of the number field that shows and reads the value as base-16 text; it is not a different value, only a different way of writing the same number.

terms.name: Largest allowed value
terms.means: The biggest number the edited value can hold, which depends on whether the value is a 32-bit or a 64-bit number; it is not a limit on how many digits can be typed.

criteria.says: Given the number field is showing a value and hexadecimal mode is on, when the value is shown, then it appears as hexadecimal text, including values above 7FFFFFFF.
Given hexadecimal mode is off, when the value is shown or a number is typed, then the field behaves like an ordinary number field.
Given hexadecimal mode is on, when someone types a valid hexadecimal number and leaves the field, then the value becomes that number and the field shows it again as hexadecimal text.

Given hexadecimal mode is on, when someone types a hexadecimal number too large to fit, then the value is set to the largest allowed value; and when the text is not a hexadecimal number, then the value stays unchanged.
Given the rule for oversized and non-hexadecimal text, when the tests run, then a test named after the rule passes for too-large text, non-hexadecimal text and a valid number.
Given the screen that edits a number value is open, when someone switches hexadecimal mode on, then the screen offers the hexadecimal field and passes an accessibility check.

open: Should hexadecimal text be shown in capital letters without a prefix, as the current program does?
What should happen when someone types a minus sign in hexadecimal mode: leave the value unchanged, or set the smallest value?

title: Load policy definitions from a folder or a single file
what: A person adds a set of policy definition files, or one file, to the working set of loaded definitions, or clears that set.
why: Every other view needs loaded definitions; people must be able to start fresh or build up from several sources and learn which files were refused.

terms.name: Workspace
terms.means: The set of policy definitions currently loaded; it is not the saved policy settings.

terms.name: Definitions folder
terms.means: The folder of template files remembered for the next start; it is not a single added file.

journey.name: Load policy definitions
steps: Choose to open a folder of definitions or a single template file
Choose whether to clear the workspace first (folder only)
See any problems found while loading
Browse the loaded definitions

criteria.says: Given a folder of definitions is chosen with "clear workspace" chosen, when it loads, then the workspace is emptied first and only that folder's definitions are shown; given it is not chosen, then they are added to the workspace and problems are reported without stopping the load.

Given a folder load fails, when the person is told "The folder could not be fully added to the workspace." with the reason, then the workspace may already be emptied or partly filled, the remembered folder is unchanged and the view is rebuilt anyway.

Given a folder was loaded, when "clear workspace" was chosen and the load did not fail, then it is remembered as the definitions folder for the next start; when the workspace was added to, the remembered folder is unchanged.

Given a single ADMX file is picked (ADMX files only), when it loads, then it is added to the workspace without emptying it and is not remembered; if it fails the person sees "The ADMX file could not be added to the workspace." with the reason.
Given a template file is loaded alone, when it is accepted, then it is added to the policies already loaded and the structures are built; when it is refused, one failure is reported.
Given definitions are loaded, when the person closes the workspace, then it empties at once with no confirmation and the view is rebuilt.

open: The legacy program picks folders and files from the person's disk and remembers a definitions folder; with upload through the service, what is remembered for the next start?

title: Browse categories and policies and read their descriptions
what: A person selects a category in the tree, sees its subcategories and policies in the list, highlights an item to read its description, and opens it by double-click or Enter.
why: This is the main way to find a policy among thousands.

terms.name: Current category
terms.means: The category whose contents fill the list; it is not the highlighted row.

terms.name: Selected policy
terms.means: The policy last highlighted in the list; it is not the policy being edited.

journey.name: Browse policies
steps: Pick a category in the tree
Scan its subcategories and policies in the list
Highlight an item to read its description
Open a category or a policy

criteria.says: Given a category in the tree, when the person selects it, then it becomes the current category, any selected policy is cleared, and its subcategories, policies and description are shown.

Given the policy list, when the person highlights a policy, then it becomes the selected policy and any highlighted category is cleared; highlighting a category does the reverse and highlighting nothing clears both; the description follows the highlight.

Given the policy list, when the person double-clicks or presses Enter, then with no selection nothing happens, a category opens as the current category, and a policy opens its editor for the area currently shown.

Given the window or panes are resized, when the policy name column and the description pane resize, then the name column fills the list and the description labels fit the pane width with no horizontal scroll bar.

title: Choose which categories and areas the list shows
what: A person switches empty categories on or off and chooses to see user policies, computer policies or both.
why: People work on one area at a time and need to hide clutter.

terms.name: Area
terms.means: The section a policy applies to, user or computer; it is not a category.

criteria.says: Given the "Empty Categories" menu, when the person switches it, then empty categories are shown or hidden and the view moves to the nearest visible category.
Given the area choice, when the person picks "User", then user policies show; "Computer" shows computer policies; any other choice shows both.

title: Merge identical user and computer policy pairs
what: A person merges policy pairs that are the same for users and computers into single policies applying to both.
why: Templates often define the same setting twice; one entry per setting is easier to browse.

terms.name: Deduplication
terms.means: Merging identical user and computer policy pairs into one; it is not deleting policies.

criteria.says: Given two policies alone in the same category under the same name, one for users and one for computers, with the same explanation text and registry key, when deduplicating, then the first is removed and the second applies to both sections.
Given the person chooses to deduplicate, when it finishes, then they are told "Deduplicated N policies." with the number merged.

title: Open the lists of loaded files, support rules and products
what: A person opens the list of loaded template files, of all support rules, or of all products.
why: People need to see what is loaded to understand what policies they can browse.

criteria.says: Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses the loaded files list, then the template files in the workspace are listed.
Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses all support rules, then every support rule is listed.
Given loaded definitions, when the person chooses all products, then the top-level products are listed ordered by name, each with its number of children.

title: Use the right-click menu on categories and policies
what: A person right-clicks a category or policy and picks an action that applies to it.
why: The menu gives quick access to opening, editing, details and inspection.

criteria.says: Given a right-click, when the menu opens, then it shows only actions that fit: policy-only actions are hidden for a category and category-only actions for a policy.

Given the menu opens from the category tree it applies to the selected category; from elsewhere with a policy-list row selected it applies to that row; from elsewhere with no row selected it is not shown.
Given a category in the tree is right-clicked, when the menu opens, then it becomes the selected category; a left-click is left as is.
Given the menu is open, when the person chooses an item, then the category, edit window, details window or inspection window opens for the chosen object.

open: The legacy program fails with an error when the menu opens from the category tree with no selected category; what should the person see instead?

title: Open a loaded template file's details from the file list
what: A person opens the details of a template file from the list of loaded files, by double-click or Enter, and sees only what that file defined.
why: It shows which policies, categories, products and support rules each file contributes.

terms.name: Template file
terms.means: An ADMX file of policy definitions; not the language file with its texts.

criteria.says: Given the loaded files list, when the person double-clicks a row, then that file's details open without checking a row is selected; pressing Enter checks first.
Given a template file's details, when they open, then only policies, categories (with sub-categories), products (with versions) and support rules defined in that file are listed.
Given the window changes size, when it resizes, then the namespace column fills the width left over.

open: Double-clicking with no row selected is unchecked in the legacy program; should it do nothing, like Enter?

title: Browse products by version and open product details
what: A person picks a product, then a major version, then sees the minor versions, and opens product details.
why: Products form a three-level tree and people filter policies by them.

terms.name: Major version
terms.means: A first-level revision of a product; not a minor version.

terms.name: Minor version
terms.means: A revision beneath a major version.

criteria.says: Given a top-level product is selected, when the major versions list fills, then it shows its children ordered by version, with the heading naming the product; with none selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.
Given a major version is selected, when the minor versions list fills, then it shows its children ordered by version, with the heading naming it; with none selected it is empty and prompts for one.
Given a list of products, when the person double-clicks or presses Enter, then product details open; with no product selected nothing happens.

title: Filter the support rules list and open support rule details
what: A person types text to narrow the support rules and opens the details of one, by double-click or Enter.
why: There are many support rules and people look one up by name.

terms.name: Support rule
terms.means: A named condition listing the products a policy runs on; not a policy.

criteria.says: Given the support rules list, when the person double-clicks a row, then its details open without checking a row is selected; Enter checks first.

Given typed filter text, when the list updates, then only names containing it, ignoring case, show; an empty filter shows all; entries are ordered by name ignoring leading spaces and shown without them.

open: Double-clicking with no row selected is unchecked in the legacy program; should it do nothing, like Enter?

title: Open details of a policy, category, product or support rule
what: From a template file's details window, a person opens the details of a policy, category, product or support rule by double-click, and reads how policies relate to categories, support rules and areas.
why: It explains where each item sits, including when its category or support rule is unknown.

terms.name: Orphaned
terms.means: Naming a parent or category that is not loaded; not the same as having none.

criteria.says: Given a policy in a category that exists, when its details open, then the category name shows and the category button is enabled; an unknown category shows "<orphaned from " plus the code, none shows "<uncategorized>", and the button is disabled.

Given a policy naming a support rule that exists, when its details open, then its name shows and the support button is enabled; if missing it reads "<missing: " plus the code, with no code blank, and the button is disabled.
Given a policy, when its details open, then it names the section: "User or computer", "Computer" or "User".

Given a category, when its details open, then the parent name shows and the button is enabled; a missing named parent shows "<orphaned from <parent>>" and disables it; a top-level category shows nothing.
Given a list of policies, categories, products or support rules in file details, when a row is double-clicked, then the matching details window opens.

title: Move from a category to its parent category
what: A person opens a category's parent from the category details window.
why: It lets people walk up the category tree.

criteria.says: Given a category's details with a parent, when the person presses the parent button, then the parent's details show in the same window.

title: Open category and support rule details from policy details
what: A person opens the details of a policy's support rule or category from the policy details window.
why: They can see where a policy applies and what it needs.
